गा। 


और जबकि उक्त आवेदक ने सक्षम प्राधिकारी की क्षतिपूर्ति करने के लिए आगे भी सहमति व्यक्त की है; यह क्षतिपूर्ति उन किसी 
भी दावों के संबंध में होगी जो प्राधिकारी के विरुद्ध क्षति, मुआवजा या किसी अन्य रूप में प्रस्तुत किए जा सकते हैं विशेषकर तब, 
जब प्राधिकारी को किसी व्यक्ति, या आस-पास की संपत्तियों के आवेदक/आवेदकों को ऐसी कोई रकम भुगतान करने की 
आवश्यकता पड़े। आवेदक इसके द्वारा सहमति देता है/वचन देता है और यह दायित्व लेता है कि वह प्राधिकारी की पूर्ण रूप से

पूरी रकम का भुगतान करेगा। 


आवेदक इसके द्वारा आगे यह वचन देते हैं और सहमति व्यक्त करते हैं कि वे सक्षम प्राधिकारी की किसी भी ऐसी रकम के लिए 
क्षतिपूर्ति करेंगे जिसका भुगतान प्राधिकारी को मुआवजे, क्षतिपूर्ति या किसी अन्य मद के रूप में करना पड़ सकता है; इसके 
अतिरिक्त, वे प्राधिकारी की उन समस्त लागतों और wal के लिए भी क्षतिपूर्ति करने का वचन देते हैं, जो प्राधिकारी को किसी भी 
न्यायालय में ऐसे किसी मामले की पैरवी (बचाव) करने हेतु वहन करने पड़ सकते हैं। आवेदक यह वचन देता है कि प्लॉट की

उपर्युक्त तथ्यों, तथा Sat आवेदक द्वारा दिए गए वचन और क्षतिपूर्ति के आश्वासन के दृष्टिगत, सक्षम प्राधिकारी इसके द्वारा उक्त

cubic content or any room or rooms; or 


(c) The conversion of any passage or space in such building into a room or rooms.

PROCEDURE FOR SANCTION OF BUILDING PLANS AND RELATED 
DOCUMENTATION 


BUILDING SANCTION REQUIRED.—No person shall carry out any erection, re-erection, 
addition or alteration to any building or cause the same to be done without obtaining a 
sanction for such work from the Competent Authority. 


PROCEDURE FOR OBTAINING BUILDING SANCTION.—(/) An applicant who intends to 
erect or re-erect a building or to make addition or alteration in any building shall register 
himself/herself in the e-Chhawani portal and apply through online, duly enclosing all the 
requisite documents and plans, in e-Chhawani portal through Cantonment Board, Ramgarh 
registered architect/engineer: 


Provided that due to any reasons, if it is not feasible for an applicant to apply in the e- 
Chhawani portal the Board may prescribe a procedure for submission of applications:

submission of photographs to this effect. The quantum of incentive for different categories of 
buildings shall be decided by the Board by resolution. 


Stacking of building material on street or other public land shall not take place without the 
permission of the Chief Executive Officer on a case-to-case basis and on payment of charges 
as fixed by the Chief Executive in terms of Section 257 of the Act.

submitted through online on e-Chhawani portal at the time of submitting application for building

(i) Proof of ownership / HOR/ Lessee / Successor / legal rights document.

PROCEDURE.— () In case of old grant land, the proposed building plan shall be in conformity

(i) That the building or the use of the site for the building or any of the particulars 
comprised in the site plan, ground plan, elevation, section or specification 
contravenes the provisions of the Act or the Bye-Laws made thereunder; 


(ii) That the notice for sanction does not contain the particulars or is not prepared in the 
manner required under the provisions of these Bye-Laws; 


(iii) That any information or documents required by the Board under these Bye-Laws has 
or have not been duly furnished; 


(iv) That the building plan is not in accordance with the bye-laws framed by the Board 
under section 260 or those framed under clauses (9) and (20) of section 348 of the 
Act; 

(v) That the building would be an encroachment on defence land or land vested in the 


Cantonment Board; 


(vi) That the site of the building does not abut on a street or projected street and that 
there is no access to such building from any such street by a passage or path-way 
appertaining to such site; 


(vii) That the erection or re-erection of the building is not in conformity with any general 
scheme sanctioned under Section 240 of the Act; 


(viii) When the land on which it is proposed to erect or re-erect the building is entrusted to 
the management of the Board by the Government if the erection or re-erection 
constitutes a breach of terms of the entrustment of management or contravenes any 
of the instructions issued by the Government regarding the management of the land 
by the Board; 


(ix) When the land on which it is proposed to erect or re-erect the building is not held ona 
lease from the Government, if the right to build on such land is in dispute between the

REVOCATION OF SANCTIONED BUILDING PLANS AND LIABILITY OF THE APPLICANT 
TO CONFORM TO BYE-LAWS.— (!) The Competent Authority may revoke any building 
sanction issued under the provisions of these bye-laws, whenever there has been any false 
statement or any misrepresentation of material fact, or concealment of facts in the application 
on which the building sanction was based, and the whole work executed on the basis of such 
sanction shall be treated as unauthorized. Further, any or all executed works in cases of 
deviation from the sanctioned plan shall be treated as unauthorized construction and would 
lead to revocation of accorded sanction. 


In the case of revocation of sanction during course of construction under above Bye-law, no 
compensation /damages shall be payable by the Competent Authority. 


No such order of revocation shall be passed by the Competent Authority without giving a 
reasonable opportunity to the applicant of being heard.

34. EXIT REQUIREMENTS.—() General requirements: 

(a) Every building meant for human occupancy shall be provided with exits 
sufficient to provide for safe escape of occupants in case of fire or other emergency; 

(b) In every building, exit shall comply with the minimum requirement of this part, 
except those not accessible for general public use; 

(c) All exits shall be free of obstructions; 

(d) No building shall be altered so as to reduce the number, width or protection of exits 
to less than that required; 

(e) Exits shall be clearly visible and the routes to reach the exit shall be clearly 
marked and sign posted to guide the population of floor concerned; 

(f) All exit ways shall be properly illuminated; 

(g) Fire fighting equipment where provided along exits shall be suitably located and 
clearly marked but must not obstruct the exit way and yet there should be clear 
indication about its location from either side of the exit way; 

(h) Alarm devices shall be installed to ensure prompt evacuation of the population 
concerned through the exits, wherever required; 

(i) All exits shall provide continuous means of egress to the exterior of a building or 
to an exterior open space leading to a street; 

(j) Exits shall be so arranged that they may be reached without passing through 
another occupied unit, except in the case of residential buildings. 

(2) Types of Exits: (a) Exits shall be either of horizontal or vertical type. An exit may be 
doorway, corridor passageways, ramp, internal staircase or external staircase, to an internal 
or external open area, verandah and/or terraces which have access to the street or to roof of 
a building; 

(b) An exit may also include a horizontal exit leading to an adjoining building at the same 
level; and 

(c) Lifts, escalators and revolving doors shall not be considered as exits. 

(3) Number and Size of Exits: The requisite number and size of various exits shall be 


provided, based on the population in each room, area and floor based on the occupant 
load, capacity of exits, travel distance and height of buildings- 


(a) Arrangement of Exits: Exits shall be so located that the travel distance on the 
floor shall not exceed 22.50 metres for residential, educational, institutional and 
hazardous occupancies and 30.00 metres for assembly, business, mercantile, 
industrial and storage occupancies. Whenever more than one exit is required for a 
floor of a building, exits shall be placed as remote from each other as possible. All

SEWERAGE PLAN. - Every person shall also submit a detailed sewerage plan along with 
the building plan, indicating the location, size, and capacity of the septic tank/soak pit, 
dimensions of sewer lines, size of manholes, and the layout of existing and proposed 
sewerage system. The use of dry latrines is strictly prohibited. The applicant shall ensure 
that the system provides proper discharge of sewage, minimizes the risk of contamination, 
prevents leakage/leaching and the accumulation of solids and odorous waste. Septic tanks 
shall be appropriately sized to accommodate the number of occupants, be fully watertight 
and provided with properly designed inlets and outlets. Sewer lines shall be of suitable 
material (as per prevalent IS code) and diameter, laid at proper slope and depth, with 
manholes provided at junctions, bends, and at regular intervals for inspection and 
maintenance. Layouts shall avoid trees, foundations, water and gas pipelines, etc. 
Connection to the main sewer line of Cantonment shall be made wherever feasible, subject 
to capacity verification of the main sewer line. Local treatment via septic tank and soak pit 
shall be provided in cases where the main sewer line does not exist or where it is not 
feasible to connect the building sewerage system with the main sewer line. Under no 
circumstances shall fecal matter/sludge/sewage be discharged into open drains, nallahs, 
natural water sources or any other water bodies.

SAVINGS, PENALTIES AND INTERPRETATION

the buildings erected as per the building plans approved by the Board before the date of 
entry into force of this Bye-laws shall also be valid.

punishable as per the provisions of the Act.

POLICIES.—Notwithstanding anything contained hereunder, the provisions of this Building 
Bye- Laws shall at all times be in consonance and within the provisions of the Act and other 
statutory rules under the Act. Wherever any discrepancy or ambiguity arises, the Act shall 
apply and shall prevail. The provisions of the Act, 2006 are in-built into these Bye-Laws and 
shall be read as part of the Bye-Laws for understanding and applying the Bye-Laws. Similarly, 
the terms of lease, terms of old grant and such other terms as per the existing policies or any 
policy issued in this regard from time to time shall prevail and the Building Bye- Laws now 
promulgated shall be within the meaning of these policies and shall not be in any way contrary 
to the said policy terms. To the said extent, the terms of these Building Bye-Laws are 
conditional.

BUILDING SANCTION REQUIRED: No person shall carry out any erection, re-erection,

4. 


PROCEDURE FOR OBTAINING BUILDING SANCTION -  ({) An applicant who intends 
to erect or re-erect a building or to make addition or alteration in any building shall register 
himself/herself in the e-Chhawani portal and apply through online, duly enclosing all the 
requisite documents and plans, in e-Chhawani portal through Cantonment Board 
registered architect/ engineer: 


Provided that due to any reasons, if it is not feasible for an applicant to apply in the e- 
Chhawani portal, the Board may prescribe a procedure for submission of applications:

guidelines from time to time to the Board regarding the manner of submitting applications

involved, the Board shall have the right to refuse or reject applications for erections,

regularized or condoned. 


(3) On scrutiny of the documents and plans submitted, the applicant receives the 
development charges communication (or the charges levied by the Board by whatever 
name these are known) for payment to Cantonment Board.

New Delhi, the 15th October, 2026 


G.S.R. 895(E).— In exercise of the powers conferred by section 55 of the Special Economic Zones 
Act, 2005 (28 of 2005), the Central Government hereby makes the following rules further to amend the 
Special Economic Zones Rules, 2006, namely: — 


1. Short title and commencement. - (/) These rules may be called the Special Economic Zones (Fourth 
Amendment) Rules, 2026. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 


2. In the Special Economic Zones Rules, 2006 (hereinafter referred to as the said rules), in rule 18, in 
sub-rule (2), after clause (ii), the following clauses shall be inserted, namely: - 


“(ii a) For the purpose of a fund setup in any International Financial Service Centre, the provisional 
offer of space confirmed by the Developer in writing for the fund management entity shall be 
considered as the provisional offer of space. 


Explanation 1.— For the purpose of this clause, (ii b) and proviso to sub-rule (3) of rule 22, the 
expressions “fund management entity (FME)” and "fund" shall have the same meanings as 
respectively assigned to them in clauses (n) and (gg) of regulation 2 of the International Financial 
Services Centres Authority Regulations, 2025. 


Explanation 2.— For the purpose of this clause, (ii b) and proviso to sub-rule (4) and sub-rule (6B) 
of rule 19, sub-rule (7) of rule 21B and proviso to sub-rule (3) of rule 22, the expression “International 
Financial Service Centre” shall have the same meaning as assigned to it in clause (g) of section 3 of 
the International Financial Services Centres Authority Act, 2019 (50 of 2019) and rules or regulations 
made thereunder. 


(ii b) For a fund setup in any International Financial Service Centre, the Lease Deed executed by the 
fund management entity of the said fund shall be considered as Lease Deed of the said fund.”. 


3. In the said rules, in rule 19, — 
(i) in sub-rule (4) after third proviso, the following proviso shall be inserted, namely: — 


“Provided also that for a Unit set up in an International Financial Service Centre, grant of 
the first recognition, registration, license or authorisation, by whatever name called, in its final form, 
by the International Financial Services Centres Authority, shall be considered as commencement of 
service activity and the date of commencement shall be the date of grant of such recognition, 
registration, license or authorisation: 


Provided also that the date of commencement determined under the fourth proviso shall be 
the same even if the recognition, registration, license or authorisation issued by the International

Financial Services Centres Authority based on which the commencement of the Unit was so 
determined, ceases to be valid.”; 


(ii) in sub-rule (6B), the following proviso shall be inserted, namely: — 


“Provided that for a Unit set up in an International Financial Service Centre, the renewal of 
Letter of Approval shall be decided based on the recommendations of the International Financial 
Services Centres Authority on the following criteria, namely: — 


(i) employment generated; 
(ii) instance of violation of applicable statutes related to the functioning of the Unit; and 
(iii) cases of default, if any, of statutory payments.” 

4. In the said rules, for rule 21B, the following rule shall be substituted, namely: — 


"21B. Units dealing with aircraft or ship leasing activities. — (/) A Unit in an International 
Financial Services Centre, authorised to undertake aircraft or ship leasing or a person intending to 
setup a Unit in an International Financial Services Centre to undertake aircraft or ship leasing activity, 
if allowed by the International Financial Services Centre Authority not to maintain separate office, 
may utilize office space or manpower or both, of another Unit authorised to undertake aircraft or ship 
leasing activity or Trust and Company Service Provider activity, as may be approved by the 
International Financial Services Centre Authority: 


Provided that utilisation of office space or manpower or both shall be allowed only with 
Trust and Company Service Provider, which is providing or intending to provide their services to the 
person allowed under this sub-rule. 


(2) A person allowed under the sub-rule (/) shall not require a separate provisional offer of space 
and lease deed, and as such the provisional offer of space and lease deed of the Unit with which 
office space is being shared shall suffice for the purposes of rule 18.". 


Di: In the said rules, in rule 22 after sub-rule (3), the following proviso shall be inserted, namely: — 


“Provided that nothing contained in this sub-rule shall apply to a fund setup in an 
International Financial Service Centre.’’.

सभी शक्तियां निम्नलिखित शर्तों एवं निबंधनों के अधीन प्रदान करता है, जो भारतीय टेलीग्राफ अधिनियम, 1885 के तहत 
टेलीग्राफ के प्रयोजन के लिए सरकार द्वारा स्थापित अथवा अनुरक्षित किए गए टेलीग्राफ लाइन एवं खम्भे या इस प्रकार की 
स्थापना और अनुरक्षण किए जाने के लिए, टेलीग्राफ प्राधिकरण को प्राप्त हैं: 


i, यह अनुमोदन 25 वर्षों के लिए प्रदान किया जाता है। 


1. आवेदक को प्रस्तावित लाइन के स्थापना से पूर्व संबंधित प्राधिकरणों अर्थात स्थानीय निकायों, रेलवे, राष्ट्रीय 
राजमार्गों, राज्य राजमार्गों आदि से सहमतियां प्राप्त करनी होंगी। 


ii, आवेदक को विद्युत अधिनियम, 2003 के तहत सक्षम आयोग के द्वारा तैयार किए गए ट्रांसमिशन ओ एंड एम, ओपन 
एक्सेस आदि से संबंधित विधियों/दिशानिर्देशों का पालन करना होगा। 


iv. भारत सरकार के विद्युत निरीक्षक/मुख्य विद्युत निरीक्षक के अनुमोदन के पश्चात ही लाइन का संचालन करेगा। 


५. यह अनुमोदन आवेदक द्वारा विद्युत अधिनियम, 2003 के प्रावधानों और उसके तहत बनाए गए नियमों की अपेक्षाओं

शक्तियों का प्रयोग करते हुए (जिसे आगे 'उक्त अधिनियम' कहा गया है) केंद्र सरकार, इस सार्वजनिक उद्देश्य के लिए कि 
अनुसूची में संलग्न भूमि का संक्षिप्त विवरण, “विशेष रेलवे परियोजना अर्थात्‌ बिसुगीर शरीफ और जम्मीकुंटा स्टेशनों के बीच 
कि.मी. 327/11-13 पर समपार फाटक सं.23 के स्थान पर रोड ओवर ब्रिज का निर्माण”, करीमनगर जिला, तेलंगाना राज्य 
में कार्यान्वयन के लिए आवश्यक है, इस प्रकार ऐसी भूमि को अधिग्रहीत करने के अपने अभिप्राय की घोषणा करती है। 


कोई भी व्यक्ति, जो उक्त भूमि में रुचि रखता है, वह इस अधिसूचना के राजपत्र में प्रकाशन की तिथि से तीस (30) 
दिनों की अवधि के भीतर, उक्त भूमि के अधिग्रहण और उपयोग पर धारा ZOD की उप-धारा (1) के तहत आपत्ति प्रस्तुत कर 
सकता है। 

प्रत्येक ऐसी आपत्ति सक्षम प्राधिकारी अर्थात्‌ राजस्व मंडल अधिकारी, हुज़्राबाद, करीमनगर जिला को लिखित 
रूप में की जाएगी और उसके आधार बताए जाएंगे और सक्षम प्राधिकारी तथा राजस्व मंडल अधिकारी, हुज़्राबाद, करीमनगर 
जिला, आपत्तिकर्ता को सुनवाई का अवसर देंगे, या तो व्यक्तिगत रूप से या कानूनी सलाहकार द्वारा और ऐसी सभी आपत्तियों

NOTIFICATION 
Jabalpur, the 16th October, 2026 


S.O. 5676(E).— Whereas, by the notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of Railways (West 
Central Railway, Construction Organisation), number S.O. 4760(E) dated 177 October, 2025 published in the Gazette 
of India, Extraordinary, Part II, Section-3, Sub-Section (1), and issued under the sub-section (1) of section 20A of 
the Railways Act, 1989 (24 of 1989) (hereinafter referred to as the said Act), the Central Government declared its 
intention to acquire the land specified in the schedule annexed to the said notification for execution, maintenance, 
management and operation of the Special Railway Project namely, “Construction of Road Over Bridge at level 
crossing No. 344 at KM 1052/7-8 between Dundi - Sleemnabad station of Itarsi - Katni” in Katni District in 
the State of Madhya Pradesh, hereby declares its intention to acquire such land. 

And whereas, the substance of the said notification has been published in the daily local newspapers namely, 
"The Hitavada" (in English) and "Yash Bharat" (in Hindi) on dated 26" October, 2025 under the sub-section (4) of 
section 20A of the said Act. 

And whereas, no objections were received by the Competent Authority. 

And whereas, in pursuance of sub-section (1) of section 20E of the said Act, the Competent Authority has 
submitted its report to the Central Government. 

Now therefore, upon receipt of the report of the Competent Authority and in exercise of the powers conferred 
by sub-section (1) of section 20E of the said Act, the Central Government hereby declares that the land specified in 
the schedule annexed hereto shall be acquired for the aforesaid purpose. 

And further, in pursuance of sub-section (2) of section 20E of the said Act, the Central Government hereby 
declares that on publication of this notification in the Official Gazette, the land specified in the schedule annexed 
hereto shall vest absolutely in the Central Government free from all encumbrances.

प्रदत्त शक्तियों का प्रयोग करते हुए, राष्ट्रीय आयुर्विज्ञान आयोग एतट्ठटारा चिकित्सा शिक्षा विनियम, 2023 के मानकों के 
रखरखाव (एमएसएमईआर-2023), जिसे अधिसूचना संख्या एफ. सं. एन-पी046/॥/2023-पीजीएमईबी-एनएमसी 
दिनांक 9 सितंबर, 2023 के माध्यम से अधिसूचित किया गया था और भारत के राजपत्र, असाधारण, भाग Ill, खंड 4, 
संख्या 652, दिनांक 24 सितंबर, 2023 में प्रकाशित हुआ था, को तत्काल प्रभाव से हटाया जाता है।

प्रभावी बनी रहेगी।

3. संक्रमणकालीन और व्यावृत्ति उपबंध: चिकित्सा शिक्षा विनियम, 2023 के मानकों के रखरखाव के अधिसूचना से 
हटाए जाने के बावजूद, निम्नलिखित पर कोई प्रभाव नहीं पड़ेगा: 


(क) उक्त विनियमों के अधिसूचना से हटाए जाने की तारीख से पूर्व, उनके अधीन विधिवत की गई अथवा की गई 
मानी जाने वाली कोई भी कार्रवाई; 


(ख) उक्त विनियमों के अधिसूचना से हटाए जाने की तारीख से पूर्व, उन विनियमों के तहत विधिवत रूप से प्रदान 
किया गया कोई भी अनुमोदन, नवीनीकरण, आदेश, निर्णय या निर्देश; 


(ग) उक्त विनियमों के अधिसूचना से हटाए जाने की तारीख से पूर्व, अर्जित, उपार्जित अथवा अधिरोपित कोई भी 
अधिकार, विशेषाधिकार, दायित्व या जवाबदेही; 


घ) उनकी अधिसूचना से हटाए जाने की तारीख से ठीक पूर्व लंबित कोई भी आवेदन, कार्यवाही, अपील, जांच या 
अन्य मामला, जहाँ तक लागू हों, उक्त विनियमों के प्रावधानों के अनुसार और इस अधिसूचना के प्रावधानों के अधीन जारी 
रखा जाएगा और उसका निपटारा किया जाएगा; 


बशर्ते कि अधिसूचना से हटाए जाने की तारीख को या उसके बाद उत्पन्न होने वाले किसी भी मामले पर राष्ट्रीय 
आयुर्विज्ञान आयोग अधिनियम, 2049 और उस समय प्रवृत्त वैधानिक और विनियामक प्रावधानों द्वारा लागू होगा।

MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS 
(South Central Railway) 
NOTIFICATION 
Secunderabad, the 16th October, 2026 

S.O. 5679(E).— In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (1) of Section 20A of the Railways Act, 
1989 (24 of 1989) (hereafter referred as in as the said Act), the Central Government after being satisfied that for the 
public purpose, the land, the brief description of which is given in the schedule annexed here to, is required for 
execution of the Special Railway Project, Doubling of track between Mudkhed - Medchal Sections (221.06 Kms) in 
Medak District, Telangana State, hereby declares its intention to acquire such land. 


Any person interested in the said land may, within a period of thirty (30) days from the date of publication of 
this notification in the official gazette, raise objection to the acquisition and use of such land for the aforesaid purpose 
under sub-section (1) of Section 20-D of the said Act. 


Every such objection, shall be made to the Competent Authority (LA), namely Land Acquisition Officer & 
Revenue Divisional Officer, Toopran Division in writing and shall be set out the grounds there of and the Competent 
Authority and Revenue Divisional Officer, Toopran Division shall give the objector an opportunity of being heard, 
either in person or by legal practitioner and may, after hearing all such objections and after making such further 
enquiry, if any as the Competent Authority (LA) thinks necessary, by order, either allow or disallow the objections. 


Any order made by the Competent Authority under sub section (2) of section 20(D) of the said act shall be 
final. 


The land plans and other details of the land under this notification are available and can be inspected by the 
interested persons at the aforesaid office of the competent authority.

New Delhi, the 16th October, 2026 
S.O. 5673(E).— Whereas, the use of Aadhaar number to establish identity enables individuals to receive 
subsidies, benefits and services in a convenient and seamless manner, obviates the need for multiplicity of documents 
to establish identity, simplifies processes and promotes transparency and efficiency; 


And whereas, the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment (hereinafter referred to as the said 
Department) in the Government of India (hereinafter referred to as the said Government) is administering the Pre- 
Matric Scholarships Scheme for Scheduled Castes and Others through State Governments and Union territory 
Administrations (hereinafter referred to as the said scheme); 


And whereas, scholarship is given to the Scheduled Castes students and children whose parents or guardians are 
engaged in unclean and hazardous occupation (hereinafter referred to as the said benefit) under the said scheme and 
the instructions and guidelines issued in respect thereof ; 


And whereas, expenditure for the said scheme is incurred from the Consolidated Fund of India; 


And whereas, the said Government, for the purpose of establishing the identity of a beneficiary as a condition 
for the receipt of the said benefit, requires that such beneficiary undergoes authentication, or furnishes proof of

possession of Aadhaar number or in the case of an individual to whom no Aadhaar number has been assigned to, make 
an application for such enrolment; 


Now, therefore, in pursuance of the provisions of section 7 of the Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and 
Other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016 (18 of 2016), the Government of India hereby notifies the 
following, namely: — 


1. (1) An individual desirous of availing of the said benefit under the said scheme shall be required to undergo 
authentication, or furnish proof of possession of Aadhaar number. 


(2) In case such an individual has not been assigned an Aadhaar number, he shall be required to make an 
application for enrollment: 


Provided that if that individual is a child, such application shall be made only with the consent of his parent 
or legal guardian. 


(3) In accordance with the provisions of regulation 12 of the Aadhaar (Enrollment and Update) Regulations, 
2016, the said Department shall ensure enrollment of such beneficiaries who are yet to be enrolled, or update their 
Aadhaar details through appropriate measures, including coordination with Registrars and setting up enrollment 
centres at convenient locations or providing enrollment facilities by becoming a Registrar itself: 


Provided that till such time an Aadhaar number is assigned to such beneficiary, he may establish his identity to 
avail the said benefit, by presenting the following documents to which he is entitled and which are valid at the time of 
presentation, or, in case the software provided or authorised by the said Department for such identification supports 
electronic obtaining of information evidencing the contents of such documents from the database of the authorities 
dealing with the preparation or maintenance thereof, by giving his consent for so obtaining, namely: — 


For a child below eighteen years of age to whom an Aadhaar number has not been assigned:- 


(a) the acknowledgement of the beneficiary having undergone the process of enrollment, provided by the 
operator at the enrollment centre, containing the Enrollment ID; and 


(b) any one of the following documents to evidence that the beneficiary is a child below eighteen years of 
age, namely:—

extracted from the entry made in the register of _ births regarding the birth of the beneficiary; 


(ii) Indian passport; 


(iii) certificate or statement of marks of matriculation or 10th class or higher secondary or 
12th class, issued by a recognised Board of school education;

by the person-in-charge, superintendent, Child Welfare Officer or probation officer of such institution; or 


(v) in respect of a foreign national,—

(II) if he is a Tibetan refugee, a registration certificate issued by a Foreigners Regional Registration

(11) if he is a national of Nepal or Bhutan, passport of Nepal or Bhutan;

(a) in case any particular biometric-based mode of authentication is not successful, any other mode of

accordance with the details given in this regard on the website of Unique Identification Authority of India.

MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS 
(Department of Pharmaceuticals) 
(NATIONAL PHARMACEUTICAL PRICING AUTHORITYS) 
ORDER 
New Delhi, the 17th October, 2026 


S.O. 5690(E).—Whereas the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) was established vide 
Resolution No. 33/7/97-PLI dated 29th August, 1997 of the Government of India in the Ministry of Chemicals and 
Fertilizers to fix/revise and monitor prices of drugs/formulations and oversee implementation of the Drugs (Prices 
Control) Order, 2013 (DPCO, 2013); and whereas, the Government of India, vide S.O. 1349(E) dated 30th May, 2013, 
in exercise of the powers conferred by Section 3 and 5 of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 (10 of 1955) has 
delegated the powers in respect of various paragraphs including paragraph 19 of the DPCO, 2013 to the NPPA to 
exercise the functions of the Central Government. 


2. And whereas, the aim of the DPCO, 2013 issued under section 3 of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955, is to 
ensure that Essential Drugs are available to all, at affordable prices. While the prices of scheduled formulations are 
regulated through the ceiling price mechanism, non-scheduled formulations are monitored to ensure that the annual 
increase in their Maximum Retail Price (MRP) does not exceed the limit prescribed under Paragraph 20 of DPCO, 
2013. 


3. And whereas, cancer treatment in India imposes a severe financial burden on patients and their families 
resulting in catastrophic health expenditure. Serious concerns have been raised by state authorities, patients, civil 
society, and through public platforms regarding excessive pricing of anti-cancer drugs, particularly highlighting the 
wide disparity between the procurement price and the Maximum Retail Price (MRP) charged from consumers. High 
trade margin in drugs, particularly high-value anti-cancer drugs, substantially increases the financial burden on patients. 
Trade margin, for the purpose of this Order, refers to the difference between the price at which a manufacturer sells a 
formulation to a stockist/distributor (Price to Stockist/Price to Distributor) and the Maximum Retail Price (MRP) 
charged to the patient excluding Goods and Services Tax (GST). 


4. And whereas, the National List of Essential Medicines, 2022 comprises 388 drugs, including 63 anti-cancer 
drugs, which are subject to price control under DPCO, 2013. 


5. And whereas, analysis of market data indicates that the average trade mark-up in non-scheduled anti-cancer 
drugs is significantly high in certain cases. Differences have also been observed between prices charged through retail 
and hospital, including varying discounts on MRP. Such variations indicate that the MRP and the actual transaction 
price may differ considerably, and excessive trade mark-ups in oncology drugs materially increase patients’ 
expenditure. 


6. And whereas, the Government had undertaken a Trade Margin Rationalisation (TMR) as a pilot “Proof of 
Concept” basis intervention in 2019 in respect of 42 non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs by invoking the extraordinary 
powers under Paragraph 19 of DPCO, 2013. The 2019 intervention was reported to have resulted in substantial savings. 


7. And whereas, the Authority, in its 283" (overall) and 151%‘ meeting under DPCO, 2013 held on 87 October, 
2026, deliberated upon the need to address excessive trade mark-ups in non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs and observed 
that extraordinary circumstances warrant intervention under Paragraph 19 of DPCO, 2013 in public interest to address 
market distortions, curb profiteering and ensure fair and affordable prices. 


8. And whereas, the Department of Pharmaceuticals had requested the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare to 
constitute an Expert Committee under the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) to prepare a list of anti- 
cancer drugs to be covered under the proposed exercise. The Expert Committee of Ministry of Health and Family 
Welfare (MoHFW) after examining in detail, deliberating and considering all available information/data/viewpoints 
and all relevant options for ensuring affordability of essential drugs to the patients, in case of anti-cancer drugs, has 
recommended 137 non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs for TMR which are specified in Table B. This list will be updated 
periodically, as warranted by market developments and public-health considerations. 


9, The Authority, in its 284" (overall) and 152™ meeting under DPCO, 2013 held on 16" & 17" October, 2026 
considered the recommendation of the Expert Committee and the list of 137 non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs and 
decided to notify the same for coverage under TMR. The Authority noted that as per DPCO 2013, there is no restriction 
on the price fixation of the patented drugs except if exemption has been approved under Paragraph 32. Therefore, the 
Authority decided that patented drugs should also be covered under this Order. 


10. Now, therefore, in the exercise of the powers vested by the Government of India in the Ministry of Chemicals 
and Fertilizers and being satisfied that extraordinary circumstances exist and that intervention is necessary in public 
interest, the provisions of Paragraph 19 of DPCO, 2013 are hereby invoked in respect of 137 non-scheduled anti- 
cancer drugs specified in Table B below.

violation of this Order is required to be brought to the notice of NPPA. In case of violation, NPPA shall initiate 
action for recovery of overcharged amount in accordance with extant provisions of DPCO, 2013. 


The prices fixed under this Order shall remain in force until further orders. However, manufacturers may avail 
annual price increase in accordance with the provisions of Paragraph 20(1) of the Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 
2013, subject to continued compliance with the maximum permissible trade margin specified herein, from the 
date of publication of this Order in the Official Gazette. 


The manufacturers not complying with the provisions of this order shall be liable to deposit the overcharged 
amount along with interest thereon under the provisions of the Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 2013 read with 
Essential Commodities Act, 1955. The overcharged amount shall be the difference between MRP (excluding 
GST) less MRP so computed as per Table A (excluding GST).

MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS 
(South East Central Railway) 
NOTIFICATION 
Bilaspur, the 10th October, 2026 
Notification under Section 20E of The Railway Act 1989 


5.0. 5692(E).— Whereas, by the notification of the Government of India, in the Ministry of Railways (South 
East Central Railway) number S.O. 1195 (E), dated 7 March 2026, published in the Gazette of India (Extra- 
Ordinary) Part-II section 3 sub section (ii), (hereinafter referred to as the said notification) and issued under sub- 
section (1) of section 20A of the Railway Act, 1989 (24 of 1989) (hereinafter referred to as the said Act), the Central 
Government declared its intention to acquire the land specified in the schedule annexed to the said notification for the 
purpose of execution of Special Railway Project, namely “Sardega - Bhalumuda New Double Line (37.24 KM) of 
South East Central Railway”in the state of Chhattisgarh excluding village of Dolesara, Kunjemura, Pata, Libra, 
Jhinkabahal & Budiya. 


And, whereas, the substance of the said notification no. 1143, dated 77 March 2026, was published in the 
daily newspapers, Nava Bharat (Hindi) Bilaspur edition on 20.03.2026, Times of India (English) Raipur edition on 
20.03.2026 and Navin Kadam (Hindi) Raigarh edition on 20.03.2026 under sub-section (4) of Section 20A of the said 
Act; 


And whereas, objections were received within the set time period and disposed off by the Competent 
Authority under section 20D of the said act; 


And whereas, in pursuance of sub-section (1) of Section 20E of the said Act, the Competent Authority has 
submitted her report to the Central Government; 


Now therefore, upon receipt of the said report of the Competent Authority, and in exercise of the powers 
conferred by sub-section (1) of Section 20E of the said Act, 1989, the Central Government hereby declares that the 
lands specified in the schedule annexed hereto shall be acquired for the aforesaid purpose; 


And further, in pursuance of sub-section (2) of Section 20E of the said Act, the Central Government hereby 
declares that on publication of this notification in the Official Gazette, the land specified in the Schedule annexed 
hereto shall vest absolutely with the Central Government free from all encumbrances.

अंतर्गत जारी, भारत के राजपत्र, असाधारण, भाग-||, खंड 3, उप-खंड (ii), (जिसे इसमे इसके पश्चात उक्त अधिनियम कहा

तारीख 24 अक्तूबर, 2025 (जिसे इसमे इसके पश्चात उक्त अधिसूचना कहा गया है), द्वारा उक्त अधिनियम से उपावध्द 
अनुसूची में विनिर्दिष्ट भूमी को, महाराष्ट्र राज्य के छत्रपती संभाजीनगर (औरंगाबाद) जिले में विशेष रेलवे परियोजना अर्थात 
“छत्रपती संभाजीनगर (औरंगाबाद) - परभणी दोहरिकरण परियोजना” के निष्पादन, अनुरक्षण, प्रबंधन, और प्रचालन के 
लिए आपेक्षित है, ऐसी भूमि का अर्जन करने के आशय की घोषणा की थी; 

और, उक्त अधिसूचना का सार उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 20ए की उपधारा (4) के अंतर्गत दैनिक समाचारपत्रों, 
अर्थात “लोकमत टाइम्स”, “दिव्य मराठी” और, “दैनिक भास्कर” में तारीख 26 नवंबर 2025, 27 नवंबर 2025 और, 28 
नवंबर 2025 को प्रकाशित किया गया था;

और, चिकलटठाणा गांव में कोई आपत्ति प्राप्त नही हुई तथा सक्षम प्राधिकारी द्वारा तदनुसार आदेश पारित कर दिये 
गए है. 

और, गाढेजछगाव, मुकुंदवाडी, TSS काजी, हसनाबादवाडी और करमाड गांव मे कुछ आपत्तियां प्राप्त हुई थीं तथा 
उन्हें सक्षम प्राधिकारी द्वारा विचारोपरांत तदनुसार आदेश पारित कर दिये गए है. 


और, उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 20ई की उपधारा (4) के अनुसरण में सक्षम प्राधिकारी ने इसकी रिपोर्ट केंद्र सरकार 
को प्रस्तुत कर दी है; 


अतः अब केंद्र सरकार, सक्षम प्राधिकारी से उक्त रिपोर्ट के प्राप्त होने पर और उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 20 ई की 
उपधारा (॥) द्वारा प्रदत शक्तियों का प्रयोग करते हुए, यह घोषणा करती है की इससे उपाबध्द अनुसूची में विनिर्दिष्ट भूमि 
पूर्वोक्त प्रयोजन के लिए अर्जित की जाएगी; 

और यह कि केंद्र सरकार उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 20ई कि उप-धारा (2) के अनुसरण में यह घोषणा करता है कि 


आधिकारिक राजपत्र में इस अधिसूचना के प्रकाशित होने पर इससे उपाबध्द अनुसूची में विनिर्दिष्ट भूमि सभी विलंगमो से 
मुक्त होकर केंद्र सरकार में आत्यांकित रूपसे निहित हो जाएगी।

NOTIFICATION 
Secunderabad, the 7th October, 2026 


9.0. 578(E).— Whereas, by the notification of the Government of India, in the Ministry of Railways (Railway 
Board), number, 8.0. 4853(E) dated the 2 October 2025 published in Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, section 
3 Sub-section(ii), dated the 2 October 2025 (hereinafter referred to as the said notification) and issued under sub- 
section (l) of section 20(A) of the Railway Act, 989 (24 of 989), the Central Government declared its intention to 
acquire the land specified in the schedule annexed to the said notification for the purpose of execution, maintenance, 


management and operation of Special Railway Project, namely “Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad) — 
Parbhani Doubling project” in the District of Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad) in the State of Maharashtra. 
And whereas, the substance of the said notification was published in daily News Paper " Lokmat Times” “Divya 


Marathi” & “Dainik Bhaskar" dated 26 November 2025, 27 November 2025 & 28 November 2025 under sub 
section (4) of section 20A of the said Act, 


And whereas, in Chikalthana villages, objections were not received and accordingly report have been passed by the 
Competent Authority; 

And whereas, in Gadhejalgaon, Mukundwadi, Varud Kazi, Hasnabadwadi & Karmad villages certain objections were 
received and the same have been considered by the competent Authority accordingly orders have been passed; 

And whereas, in pursuance of sub-section (|) of 20E of the said Act, the competent authority has submitted its report 
to the Central Government; 

Now therefore, upon receipt of the report of the Competent Authority and in exercise of the powers conferred by sub- 
section () of section 20(E). of the said Act, the Central Government hereby declares that the lands specified in the 
schedule annexed hereto shall be acquired for the aforesaid purpose} 

And further, in pursuance of sub-section (2) of section 20E of the said Act, the Central Government hereby declares 


that on publication of this notification in the official Gazette, the land specified in the schedule annexed hereto shall 
vest absolutely in the Central government free from all encumbrances.

MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 21st October, 2026 


S.O. 5733(E).— In exercise of powers conferred by sub-section (1) of section 3A of the National Highways 
Act, 1956 (48 of 1956) (hereinafter referred to as the said Act), the Central Government, after being satisfied that for 
the public purpose, the land, the brief description of which is given in the Schedule below, is required for building 
(widening/two lane with paved shoulder/four laning etc.,), maintenance, management and operation of Greenfield 
Highway in the stretch of land from Km. 215 to Km. 342.45 (Ongole Prakasam District) in the district of PRAKASAM 
in the state of ANDHRA PRADESH, hereby declares its intention to acquire such land. 


Any person interested in the said land may, within twenty-one days from the date of publication of this 
notification in the Official Gazette, object to the use of such land for the aforesaid purpose under sub-section(1) of 
section 3C of the said Act. 


Every such objection shall be made to the Competent Authority, namely, JC Prakasam in writing and shall set 
out the grounds thereof and the Competent Authority shall give the objector an opportunity of being heard, either in 
person or by a legal practitioner, and may, after hearing all such objections and after making such further enquiry, if 
any, as the Competent Authority thinks necessary, by order, either allow or disallow the objections. 


Any order made by the Competent Authority under sub-section (2) of section 3C of the said Act shall be final. 


The land plans and other details of the land to be acquired under their notification are available and can be 
inspected by the interested person at the aforesaid office of the Competent Authority.

S.O. 5727(E).— In exercise of powers conferred by sub-section (l) of section 3A of the National Highways 
Act, 956 (48 of 956) (hereinafter referred to as the said Act), the Central Government, after being satisfied that for 
the public purpose, the land, the brief description of which is given in the Schedule below, is required for building 
(widening/two lane with paved shoulder/four laning etc.,), maintenance, management and operation of NH-5! in the 
stretch of land from Km 74.000 to Km [77.747 (Taluka Ranpur From Km. |27.300 to Km. 48.450) in the district of 
BOTAD in the state of GUJARAT, hereby declares its intention to acquire such land. 


Any person interested in the said land may, within twenty-one days from the date of publication of this 
notification in the Official Gazette, object to the use of such land for the aforesaid purpose under sub-section() of 
section 3C of the said Act. 


Every such objection shall be made to the Competent Authority, namely, SUB DIVISIONAL MAGISTRATE, 
Barwala in writing and shall set out the grounds thereof and the Competent Authority shall give the objector an 
opportunity of being heard, either in person or by a legal practitioner, and may, after hearing all such objections and 
after making such further enquiry, if any, as the Competent Authority thinks necessary, by order, either allow or disallow 
the objections. 


Any order made by the Competent Authority under sub-section (2) of section 3C of the said Act shall be final. 


The land plans and other details of the land to be acquired under their notification are available and can be 
inspected by the interested person at the aforesaid office of the Competent Authority.

New Delhi, the 21st October, 2026 


S.O. 5730(E).— In exercise of powers conferred by sub-section (1) of section 3A of the National Highways 
Act, 1956 (48 of 1956) (hereinafter referred to as the said Act), the Central Government, after being satisfied that for 
the public purpose, the land, the brief description of which is given in the Schedule below, is required for construction 
of (widening/two lane with paved shoulder/four laning etc.,), maintenance, management and operation of NH160A in 
the stretch of land from Km. 110/000 to Km. 156/000 in the district of PALGHAR in the state ofp MAHARASHTRA, 
hereby declares its intention to acquire such land. 


Any person interested in the said land may, within twenty-one days from the date of publication of this 
notification in the Official Gazette, object to the use of such land for the aforesaid purpose under sub-section(1) of 
section 3C of the said Act. 


Every such objection shall be made to the Competent Authority, namely, Sub Divisional officer Jawhar in 
writing and shall set out the grounds thereof and the Competent Authority shall give the objector an opportunity of 
being heard, either in person or by a legal practitioner, and may, after hearing all such objections and after making 
such further enquiry, if any, as the Competent Authority thinks necessary, by order, either allow or disallow the 
objections. 


Any order made by the Competent Authority under sub-section (2) of section 3C of the said Act shall be 
final. 


The land plans and other details of the land to be acquired under their notification are available and can be 
inspected by the interested person at the aforesaid office of the Competent Authority.

के लिए अनुमोदित आवेदक को प्रदत्त अनुमोदन को निलंबित या प्रतिसंह्ृृत कर सकती है, अर्थात्‌:-- 


(क) उन स्थितियों का निदान करने के लिए जहां इस तरह के सैंडबॉक्स एक प्राधिकृत इकाई द्वारा स्थापित

(ख) जहां एक अनुमोदित आवेदक ने-- 
() केन्द्रीय सरकार को गलत या मिथ्या जानकारी प्रस्तुत की है; या 
(1) उन निबंधनों और शर्तों का पालन करने में विफल रहा है जिनके आधार पर परीक्षण के लिए अनुमोदन 
प्रदान किया गया था; या 
(iii) सुसंगत विनियामक सैंडबॉक्स में प्रतिभागियों द्वारा अनुपालन सुनिश्चित करने में विफल रहा हैः

प्रतिसंहरण आवश्यक है; या 


(घ) जहां एक अनुमोदित आवेदक अधिनियम के अध्याय ४/॥॥ के उपबंधों के अधीन न्यायनिर्णयन कार्यवाही के

MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS 
(Department of Telecommunications) 
NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 21st October, 2026 


G.S.R. 905(E).— Whereas a draft of the Telecommunications (Regulatory Sandbox) Rules, 2024 was 
published, as required under sub-section (1) of section 56 of the Telecommunications Act, 2023 (44 of 2023), in the 
Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, section 3, sub-section (i), vide notification number G.S.R. 736(E), dated the 27" 
November, 2024, inviting objections and suggestions from all persons likely to be affected thereby, before the expiry of a 
period of thirty days from the date on which the copies of the Official Gazette containing the said notification were made 
available to the public: 


And whereas copies of the said Official Gazette were made available to the public on the 280 November, 2024: 


And whereas objections and suggestions received from the public in respect of the said draft rules have been 
duly considered by the Central Government: 


Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (1) and clause (y) of sub-section (2) of 
section 56 of the Telecommunications Act, 2023 (44 of 2023), the Central Government hereby makes the following 
rules, namely:— 


1. Short title and commencement.—(1) These rules may be called the Telecommunications (Regulatory Sandbox) 
Rules, 2026. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 
2. Definitions.—(1) In these rules, unless the context otherwise requires,— 
(a) “Act” means the Telecommunications Act, 2023 (44 of 2023); 


(b) “applicant” means an authorised entity or company, society or partnership firm or a statutory body, duly 
incorporated, registered or constituted under any law for the time being in force in India, or an Indian 
national, or a research and development institution recognised by the Department of Science and 
Technology, Ministry of Science and Technology, Government of India, who has submitted a proposal 
under rule 4; 


(c) “approved applicant” means an applicant approved by the Central Government or a person authorised by 
the Central Government in this behalf for the purposes of creation, operation and management of a 
regulatory sandbox; 


(d) “participant” means a participant in a regulatory sandbox that satisfies the eligibility criteria specified 
pursuant to rule 5; 


(e) “portal” means portal as referred to in rule 12; 
(f) “test users” mean the limited set of users who voluntarily participate in a regulatory sandbox; 


(g) “validity period” means the duration of the regulatory sandbox specified under sub-rule (2) of rule 5. 


8 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART I—SEC. 3(1)] 


(2) Words and expressions used in these rules and not defined herein but defined in the Act or the rules made thereunder 
shall have the meanings respectively assigned to them in the Act or the said rules. 


3. Application.—These rules provide for creation of one or more regulatory sandboxes and the terms and conditions 
applicable in respect thereof for the purposes of facilitating innovation and technological development in 
telecommunication. 


4. Creation of regulatory sandbox.—(1) The Central Government may, by order, create and specify a regulatory 
sandbox on the portal,— 


(a) suo motu, after assessing the need for the same; or 


(b) upon acceptance under sub-rule (4) of a proposal submitted by an applicant under sub-rule (2) at his own 
initiative or in response to a request for proposals from the Central Government. 


(2) An applicant may submit a proposal for a regulatory sandbox under clause (b) of sub-rule (1) in such form and 
manner and accompanied by such documents as specified on the portal, along with— 


(a) copies of reports of the limited testing undertaken by the applicant in offline or laboratory environment in 
respect of the subject matter of the application; 


(b) copies of reports of any other testing, including in experimental isolated networks; 
(c) any other information or documents as may be specified by the Central Government; 


(d) any exemptions from the requirements of authorisation or assignment or any other provision under the Act 
or rules made thereunder, or under the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997 (24 of 1997), as 
may be required for the purposes of such sandbox; and 


(e) non-refundable processing fees of ten thousand rupees. 


(3) On receipt of a proposal under sub-rule (2), the Central Government may make such inquiry as it deems fit, regarding 
the eligibility of such proposal and, for this purpose, require the applicant to furnish such information as it may call for. 


(4) The Central Government may, pursuant to the inquiry as to eligibility of the proposal received under sub-rule (2), 
either accept or reject such proposal. 


5. Terms and conditions of regulatory sandbox.—(1) For any regulatory sandbox created under rule 4, the Central 
Government may specify on the portal one or more of the following terms and conditions, namely: — 


(a) The scope and objective of the regulatory sandbox; 


(b) The name and details of one or more approved applicants responsible for operation and management of 
the regulatory sandbox and the obligations of such approved applicants; 


(c) The eligibility criteria for participants in such regulatory sandbox and the obligations of such participants; 


(d) The details of telecommunication services or telecommunication network or equipment or processes or 
technologies or products or business models that may be tested in such regulatory sandbox; 


(e) The exemptions granted from the requirements of authorisation or assignment or any other provisions 
under the Act or the rules made thereunder, or under the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997 
(24 of 1997) or the regulations made thereunder for the validity period of the regulatory sandbox: 


Provided that any exemption from the applicability of any provisions of the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India 
Act, 1997 (24 of 1997) shall be specified after prior consultation with the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India; 


(f) The risk analysis and management required to ensure mitigation of any potential risks; 


(g) The reporting requirements including those relating to the methodology of testing and steps to be taken to 
ensure compliance with the terms and conditions of the regulatory sandbox; 


(h) The validity period of the regulatory sandbox; 
(1) The details of the exit strategy for exiting the regulatory sandbox; and 


(j) The details of any other matter that in the opinion of the Central Government is relevant and connected 
with or related to the participation in such regulatory sandbox. 


(2) The validity period of a regulatory sandbox shall not exceed twenty-four months: 


[भाग 1--खण्ड 3(i)] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 9 


Provided that the Central Government may, if it considers necessary, extend the validity period for a further 
period not exceeding twelve months at a time, upon receipt of a request for extension from an approved applicant in 
such form and manner as specified on the portal, at least thirty days prior to the expiry of such validity period, 
accompanied by justification and purposes of such extension, or upon receipt of a continuation thereof under rule 8. 


6. Obligations of approved applicant.—(1) Every approved applicant shall comply with the terms and conditions of 
a regulatory sandbox specified under rule 5 for undertaking testing by itself or through other participants, in the relevant 
regulatory sandbox. 


(2) Without prejudice to the generality of sub-rule (1), every approved applicant shall— 
(a) _ establish mechanisms for— 
(i) onboarding of participants based on eligibility criteria; 
(ii) adherence by each participant to the terms and conditions of the regulatory sandbox; 


(iii) specifying the test parameters, control boundaries, testing sites and manner of maintenance of 
records of the test results by each participant; and 


(iv) monitoring and evaluating the testing undertaken by participants within the specifications 
referred to in sub-clause (iii); 


(b) ensure adherence, by itself and by every participant, with laws relating to data protection and security, and 
any other applicable law for the time being in force, when onboarding test users for testing within such 
regulatory sandbox; 


(c) provide to the Central Government information of the participants in a regulatory sandbox as well as their 
exit from such sandbox; 


(d) (i) inform such test users the purpose and scope of testing being undertaken; 


(1) obtain prior consent of the test users for being part of the test environment of the regulatory sandbox; 
and 


(iii) ensure that test users are not charged for their participation in the test environment, 


where the regulatory sandbox involves enrolment of test users for testing of telecommunication services, 
telecommunication network, equipment, processes, technologies, products or business models; 


(e) ensure that the telecommunication services or technologies or products, processes or business models 
being tested in the regulatory sandbox are not commercially available in the market during the testing 
period; 


(f) ensure storage of records relating to the testing, including work plans, methodologies, consent records of 
test users and other relevant data for a period not less than one year after expiry of validity period of the 
regulatory sandbox, and for such longer period or periods as may be determined by the Central 
Government; 


(g) ensure destruction of data and records specified under clause (f) in a secure manner; 


(h) keep the Central Government indemnified from any acts of omission or commission, breaches or any kind 
of culpability or liability arising out of or in relation to any testing in the regulatory sandbox by itself or 
by any participant; and 


(1) ensure that confidentiality is maintained, by it and the participants, with regard to the regulatory sandbox, 
including testing and results thereof: 


Provided that the Central Government may publish any relevant and generic information about the regulatory 
sandbox, including the approved applicants and participants, without revealing any proprietary information of such 
applicants or participants on the portal. 


7. Monitoring and evaluation.—(1) The Central Government may monitor and evaluate the performance of a 
regulatory sandbox created under rule 4. 


(2) For the purposes of sub-rule (1), the Central Government may— 


(a) call for such reports, information, data or records from the approved applicant as it deems fit and, for this 
purpose, require the approved applicant to furnish the same within such period of time as specified by the 
Central Government; 


10 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART I—SEC. 3(1)] 


(0). specify the format, frequency and manner in which the information or reports called for under clause (a) 
shall be furnished; and 


(c) issue such directions to the approved applicant as may be required for ensuring compliance with the terms 
and conditions of the regulatory sandbox and for protection of participants and test users. 


(3) The approved applicant shall ensure physical or virtual access to the regulatory sandbox as the Central Government 
may require and shall comply with its directions within such period of time as specified by the Central Government. 


(4) Within fifteen days of completion of testing, or at least thirty days prior to the expiry of the validity period of the 
regulatory sandbox, each approved applicant shall submit to the Central Government a comprehensive report in such form 
and manner as specified on the portal, which shall include— 


(a) the results and outcomes of the testing; 
(b) feedback from the test users, including complaints, concerns, security issues; 
(c) challenges faced during testing period; 


(d) measures taken to overcome security and other issues, consumer protection and risk mitigation measures 
deployed; 


(e) details of closure of all activities under the regulatory sandbox, along with settlement of all contractual 
and financial obligations related to all stakeholders, including participants and test users; and 


(f) any other data or information as may be specified by the Central Government. 


(5) For the purposes of monitoring and evaluation under this rule, the Central Government may, where considered 
necessary, seek the advice or assistance of one or more external experts. 


8. Continuation, modification, completion and commercialisation.—(1) On the basis of the information and reports 
furnished under rule 7, the Central Government may— 


(a) permit continuation of the regulatory sandbox for such further period and on such modified or additional 
terms and conditions as specified on the portal; or 


(b) direct completion and closure of the regulatory sandbox; or 


(c) having regard to the results of the sandbox, permit such steps as may be considered necessary for enabling 
commercial deployment of the product, service or business model in accordance with the provisions of the 
Act and the rules made thereunder. 


(2) Before taking any decision under sub-rule (1), the Central Government may seek such further information or 
clarifications as it considers necessary from the approved applicant. 


9. Suspension or revocation of approval to operate and manage regulatory sandbox.—The Central Government 
may, by order and recording the reasons therefor, suspend or revoke the approval granted to an approved applicant to 
operate and manage a regulatory sandbox in the following circumstances, namely: — 


(a) To address situations where such sandbox is interfering with the operations of a telecommunication 
network established by an authorised entity; 


(b) Where an approved applicant has— 
(i) furnished incorrect or false information to the Central Government; or 
(ii) failed to comply with the terms and conditions based on which approval for testing was granted; or 


(iii) failed to ensure compliance by participants in the relevant regulatory sandbox: 


Provided that no decision for suspension or revocation under this clause shall be made without the approved 
applicant has been given an opportunity of being heard; or 


(c) where, in the opinion of the Central Government, such suspension or revocation is necessary in the interest 
of national security or public interest; or 


(d) where an approved applicant is subject to adjudication proceedings under the provisions of Chapter VIII 
of the Act, who is held to be in breach or contravention of any rules pursuant to the adjudication 
proceedings. 


[भाग प1---खण्ड 36)] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 11 


10. Norefund of fees.—There shall be no refund of fees or charges paid in respect of the approval to operate and manage 
a regulatory sandbox under these rules, if such approval is suspended, curtailed, revoked or varied. 


11. Power to issue orders, directions or guidelines.—The Central Government may for the purposes of giving effect 
to these rules issue orders, directions or guidelines not inconsistent with the Act or these rules. 


12. Digital implementation.—The Central Government may in furtherance of section 53 of the Act, notify one or 
more portals for digital implementation of these rules, including for providing any form, manner, order, direction or 
guidelines to be specified under these rules.

C.3 Examination by the Authority 
32. The product under consideration, as defined in the initiation notification, is as follows: 
“The Product under Consideration in the present investigation is “Axle for Trailers”. The 
subject goods are manufactured and sold in different variants. However, the basic product 
characteristics and end use of all these variants remains the same and all such types of 
Trailer Axles have been covered in the scope of the PUC. All such variants essentially 
constitute a homogenous product under consideration with comparable basic characteristics 
and similar functions/uses.” 
33. The present investigation being a sunset review, the scope of the PUC is the same as the scope of the 
measure under review, i.e., the scope determined in the original investigation and retained in the first 
sunset review, including Axle for Trailers in CKD/SKD condition to which the measure was extended

The contention that the initiation notification includes drive axles is incorrect. The product under 
consideration is axles used in trailers, which are pulled by trucks or prime movers and do not have their 
own driving mechanism. Accordingly, trailer axles are non-driven axles and are distinct from drive 
axles used in trucks and prime movers, which transmit engine power to the wheels. The expression “all 
such types of Trailer Axles” in the initiation notification refers only to different types of axles used in 
trailers and does not extend the product scope to drive axles of trucks or prime movers. Therefore, the 
product covered by the initiation notification is consistent with that described in the application, and 
there is no inconsistency in the scope of the product under consideration. 

The contention that axles made from a seamless or single-piece beam constitute a different product was 
examined in the first sunset review and in the anti-circumvention investigation. The Authority had 
found that trailer axles made out of a single-piece beam and those made out of a welded beam have 
similar uses and are substitutable, and that a difference in process or technology is not a ground to 
differentiate the product when the end uses are the same. HDTPL has not brought on record any new 
fact that would justify a departure from that finding. HDTPL itself describes the imported goods as 
non-driven axles for trailers, sells the imported axles and the axles manufactured by it in India to the 
same class of customers, and states that it has been manufacturing single-tube axles in India. No 
interested party proposed a PCN or an exclusion within the time prescribed, or has quantified any 
difference in cost or price between the two variants. The Authority, therefore, does not find any ground 
to exclude such axles from the scope of the PUC. 

The Authority notes that the product under consideration includes Axles for Trailers in complete as 
well as unassembled, unfinished or incomplete form, as specified in the product scope. However, the 
import of an individual component, such as an axle tube or beam, does not automatically establish 
whether it falls within the scope of the product under consideration. This depends on the nature of the 
imported goods and the terms of the applicable customs notification. Accordingly, whether any 
particular consignment imported by HDTPL attracts anti-dumping duty is a matter for assessment by 
the Customs authorities and does not require a consignment-specific determination in the present sunset 
review. 

The Authority notes from the information on record that there is no significant difference between the 
subject goods produced by the domestic industry and those imported from the subject country. The two 
are comparable in terms of technical specifications, functions and end uses, pricing, distribution and 
marketing, and tariff classification, and are used interchangeably by consumers. The goods produced by 
the domestic industry are accordingly treated as like article to the subject goods imported from the 
subject country. 

The subject goods are classified under Chapter 87 of the First Schedule to the Customs Tariff Act, 
975, under tariff item 876 90 0. The customs classification is indicative only and is not binding on

(i) If the producers under investigation can clearly show that market economy conditions 
prevail in the industry producing the like product with regard to the manufacture,

H. ASSESSMENT OF INJURY AND CAUSAL LINK 


H.l Views of the other interested parties 
73. The following submissions have been made by the other interested parties with regard to injury and 
causal link: 

a. Nature of the examination: The burden lies on the domestic industry to establish, through positive 
evidence, that expiry of the duty is likely to lead to continuation or recurrence of dumping and 
injury. The claims of injury are speculative. 

b. Volume effect: Imports from China PR have increased only marginally over the injury period, while 
demand and the sales of the domestic industry and of the other domestic producers have increased at 
a much higher rate. Imports have fluctuated and have declined over the longer term. There is no 
volume effect. 

c. Price effect: The landed price of imports has remained stable and the net sales realisation of the 
domestic industry has increased. Price undercutting without any adverse movement in sales 
realisation does not establish injury. On HDTPL’s transactions, the landed value is above the non- 
injurious price. 

d. Economic parameters: Production, capacity utilisation, domestic and export sales, profits, cash 
profits, employment, wages and return on capital employed of the domestic industry have all 
improved over the injury period, and inventories have declined. The decline in productivity per 
employee is explained by the increase in the workforce. 

e. Financial performance of the applicant as a company: The total income and profit after tax of the 
applicant have grown substantially, it holds large cash balances, and it has expanded its capacity. 
Such performance is inconsistent with injury. Reliance is placed on the sunset review findings in 
Soda Ash from Turkey and Russia. 

f. Causal link and other factors: No causal link is established. The increase in interest and 
depreciation costs is independent of imports and must be examined separately. Other factors such as 
cyclical demand, technology, the quality and cost of component suppliers, operational inefficiency 
and intense competition from other domestic producers may have contributed to any injury. 


H.2 Views of the domestic industry 
74. The following submissions have been made by the domestic industry with regard to injury and causal 
link: 
a. Nature of the examination: The present proceeding is a sunset review and not a fresh original 
investigation. The question is whether dumping and injury are likely to continue or recur if the duty

I. CAUSAL LINK AND NON-ATTRIBUTION ANALYSIS 


The Authority has examined whether the movement in the performance of the domestic industry 
during the injury period is attributable to the subject imports or to other known factors, having regard 
to the submissions of the interested parties. 


a. Volume and value of imports from third countries: There are no imports of the subject 
goods from countries other than the subject country. 


b. Contraction in demand and changes in the pattern of consumption: Demand increased in 
2023-24 and declined thereafter. The moderation in the volumes of the domestic industry after 
2023-24 coincides with the decline in demand. No change in the pattern of consumption has 
been shown. 


८. Conditions of competition and trade restrictive practices: The sales and market share of 
the other Indian producers have increased over the injury period, while the market share of the 
domestic industry has declined. Competition among the domestic producers has thus been a 
factor in the decline in the market share of the domestic industry. 


d. Developments in technology: No evidence has been placed on record that the technology of 
the domestic industry is obsolete or that its product is not accepted in the market. 


e. Export performance: The information examined relates to the domestic sales of the 
domestic industry. Its export performance has been segregated. 


f. Productivity: Productivity per employee has declined since 2023-24. It has not prevented the 
domestic industry from earning profits. 


g. Performance of other products: The information examined is for the PUC alone. 


It follows that the moderation in the volumes and market share of the domestic industry in the period 
of investigation is attributable, to some extent, to the decline in demand and to competition from the 
other domestic producers. 


The Authority notes that in a sunset review the determination to be made is whether expiry of the 
duty is likely to lead to continuation or recurrence of dumping and injury. The fact that the domestic 
industry is not found to be suffering continued injury with the duty in force is a relevant fact, but 
does not conclude the review. The likelihood of recurrence of injury is examined hereinafter.

K. LIKELIHOOD OF CONTINUATION OR RECURRENCE OF DUMPING AND INJURY 


K. Views of the other interested parties 
09. The following submissions have been made by the other interested parties with regard to the 
likelihood of continuation or recurrence of dumping and injury: 


a. Legal standard: A second sunset review does not justify automatic continuation of the duty. A 
forward-looking assessment must rest on objective and positive evidence. Findings in earlier 
proceedings are not conclusive, and anti-dumping duty is not intended to provide indefinite 
protection. 

b. Continued dumping and trend of imports: A dumping margin cannot be treated as conclusive of 
likely injury. Imports have fluctuated, and their continued presence does not show that expiry of the 
duty would lead to a significant increase in imports at injurious prices. 

c. Surplus capacity: The combined capacity of four Chinese producers cited by the domestic industry 
does not establish that Guangdong Fuwa has surplus capacity likely to be diverted to India. 
Guangdong Fuwa operates at a high rate of capacity utilisation. The mere existence of unutilised 
capacity or inventories does not establish likelihood. 

d. Exports to third countries: The existence of exports to third countries does not establish that such 
volumes would be directed to India or would enter at dumped and injurious prices. 

e. Condition of the domestic industry: The actual improvement in the performance of the domestic 
industry must be given due weight. The domestic industry cannot rely on the remedial effect of the 
duty as a substitute for establishing likelihood.

continuation or recurrence of dumping and injury: 


a. Legal standard: The test under Section 9A(5) of the Act and Rule 23(lB) is prospective and

Condition of the domestic industry and likelihood of recurrence of injury 

The Authority notes that the domestic industry has remained profitable and has recorded positive 
cash profits and returns during the period when the anti-dumping duty has remained in force. 
However, such improvement cannot be viewed in isolation from the remedial effect of the existing 
measure. The relevant consideration in a sunset review is whether such performance is likely to be 
sustained once the measure is withdrawn. In the present case, the domestic industry continues to have 
significant unutilised capacity and remains vulnerable to lower-priced imports. The landed value of 
subject imports without anti-dumping duty is not only below the domestic selling price but also

domestic industry per unit. Consequently, any significant price reduction necessitated by intensified 
dumped imports would substantially erode, and is likely to eliminate, the profitability presently 
earned by the domestic industry. Alternatively, if the domestic industry seeks to maintain its prices, it 
is likely to suffer loss of sales volume and market share, resulting in lower production and capacity 
utilisation. Thus, the present improvement in the domestic industry’s performance reflects the 
operation of the existing remedial measure and does not diminish its vulnerability to recurrence of

Examination by the Authority 
The Authority has examined the comments submitted by the interested parties and the domestic 
industry after the Disclosure Statement. The issues raised have been considered in light of the 
verified information and the findings already recorded. The Authority's examination of the main 
issues is given below. 


i. Domestic industry and alleged related-party imports 

The Authority notes that common ownership or management does not automatically make a 
domestic producer ineligible under Rule 2(b). The documents submitted by HDTPL indicate 
relationships between certain companies but do not establish that the applicant imported the subject 
goods from China PR or that the alleged related Chinese company exported these goods to India. The 
bill of lading relates to a shipment from India to China, while the other trade records do not establish 
imports or exports of the product under consideration. The official import data also does not support 
HDTPL's claims. Further, the facts of the Wheel Loaders case are different from the present case. 
Accordingly, the Authority finds no reason to exclude the applicant from the domestic industry under 
Rule 2(b). 


ii. Product scope and standalone components 

The Authority notes that the existing product scope covers non-driven axles for trailers, including 
axles in CKD/SKD, unassembled, unfinished or incomplete form. Seamless and welded axles are 
covered where their essential characteristics, functions and uses are comparable. However, the 
import of an individual component, such as a beam or tube, does not automatically mean that it is an 
axle in CKD/SKD form. Whether anti-dumping duty applies to a particular import shall be decided 
by Customs based on the nature of the imported goods and the applicable notification. Accordingly, 
no change in the existing product scope is warranted. 


iii. Legal standard applicable to the sunset review 

The Authority notes that the present sunset review is governed by Section 9A(5) and Rule 23(B). 
Under these provisions, the main issue is whether dumping and injury are likely to continue or recur 
if the existing duty expires. Therefore, the absence of present injury or an increase in imports is not, 
by itself, sufficient to justify withdrawal of the duty. The provisions relating to original 
investigations and safeguards, as referred to by HDTPL, do not change this requirement. The 
Authority notes that the Soda Ash sunset review was decided on different facts. In that case, 
dumping margins were negative or insignificant for most subject countries, the weighted-average 
injury margins were negative, and sufficient evidence of likely recurrence of injury was not 
established. In the present case, however, dumping has continued, positive injury margins have been 
determined, and the available evidence regarding spare capacity, third-country export prices and 
likely price effects indicates a likelihood of recurrence of injury. Accordingly, the findings in the 
Soda Ash case do not alter the conclusions reached in the present review. 

iv. Import trends, injury data and non-attribution 

The Authority has examined the official transaction-wise import data from DG Systems, which 
shows that imports from China PR continued despite the existing duty. Imports after the period of 
investigation (POI) have also been considered, but only as an indication of recent trends. Regarding 
the identical indices for production and capacity utilisation, the Authority notes that these are due to 
the installed capacity remaining unchanged and do not indicate any error. Further, the injury 
assessment is based on data relating to the product under investigation. Changes in demand and 
competition from other Indian producers have also been examined separately to ensure that any 
injury caused by these factors is not attributed to dumped imports.
