v. Price undercutting and selected invoices 

The Authority has determined price undercutting by comparing the verified domestic selling 
price with the landed value of imports, excluding anti-dumping duty, on a comparable basis. 
The comparison shows positive price undercutting, indicating that imported goods were 
priced below the domestic selling price. HDTPL's calculation, which indicates negative price 
undercutting, is based on selected invoices and assumed axle weights and does not provide a 
comparable weighted-average price assessment for the period of investigation. Accordingly, 
the Authority finds no sufficient basis to revise the price undercutting determined in the 
Disclosure Statement. 


vi. Profitability and likelihood of recurrence of injury 

The Authority notes that the domestic industry has shown positive performance during the 
period when anti-dumping duty was in force. However, dumping continued during the POI. 
The available evidence also shows significant unused production capacity in China PR, 
exports to other countries at lower prices, and an existing market for Chinese exporters in 
India. These factors indicate that dumped imports are likely to increase if the duty expires. 
Such imports are likely to put pressure on domestic prices and adversely affect the domestic 
industry's performance. Accordingly, the Authority finds that expiry of the duty is likely to 
result in continuation of dumping and recurrence of material injury. 


vii. Normal value, export price and cooperation 

The Authority has calculated normal value under paragraph 7 of Annexure I, as explained in the 
earlier findings. The export price of the cooperating producer has been determined using its verified 
information after making the necessary adjustments. For producers who did not cooperate, the 
Authority has used the available information under Rule 6(8). The invoices submitted by HDTPL 
relate to other producers or different periods and do not provide a suitable basis for changing these 
calculations. Accordingly, the positive dumping margins disclosed earlier are maintained. 


viii. Requests under Rules 22 and 5 

The Authority notes that the two Chinese exporters named by HDTPL did not submit questionnaire 
responses in the present review. Merely claiming that an exporter did not export during the POI does 
not make it eligible for a new shipper review under Rule 22. Further, provisional assessment against 
a guarantee can be allowed only in a separate review under Rule 22, subject to the prescribed 
conditions and approval by the Central Government on the recommendation of the Designated 
Authority. 

Further, Rule 45, which deals with price undertakings, is not applicable to the present sunset review 
under Rule 23(3). In any case, no valid exporter-specific undertaking has been offered or examined. 
Accordingly, the requests made by HDTPL cannot be accepted in the present review. 


ix. Injury margin and continuation of duty 

The Authority has determined the non-injurious price and injury margins using the verified 
information and the method prescribed under Annexure III. These findings have been considered 
along with the evidence relating to the likelihood of future dumping and injury. In a sunset review, 
the Authority must examine what is likely to happen if the duty expires, rather than relying only on 
the injury margin during the period when duty was in force. Based on the evidence available, the 
Authority finds no sufficient reason to change the existing duty rates applicable to individual 
producers. Accordingly, continuation of the existing rates is considered appropriate.

x. Allocation of common factory expenses 

The Authority has examined the allocation of factory expenses while determining the cost of the 
product under investigation. Expenses directly related to the product have been considered 
separately, while common expenses have been allocated on a reasonable basis in accordance with 
Annexure III. The method of allocation must be appropriate to the nature of the expense and 
supported by the available records. The domestic industry has not provided sufficient verified 
information to establish that the method adopted by the Authority resulted in an incorrect cost 
calculation. Accordingly, no change is considered necessary. 


xi. Working capital and statutory deposits 

The Authority has calculated working capital for determining the non-injurious price based on the 
accepted costs and the assets and liabilities relating to the product under investigation. Regarding 
deposits with government authorities, the Authority notes that such deposits cannot be included 
merely because they appear in the company's accounts. Their inclusion depends on whether they are 
necessary for normal business operations and relate to the product under investigation. The domestic 
industry has not provided sufficient supporting calculations and records to justify their inclusion. 
Accordingly, the existing calculation is maintained. 


xii. Public interest and remaining requests 

The Authority has examined the concerns regarding the impact of anti-dumping duty on trailer 
manufacturers, availability of the product and competition in the Indian market. The evidence shows 
that other Indian producers also supply the product and does not establish any shortage caused by the 
existing duty. The estimated impact of the duty on the final price of trailers is limited, and no user 
has submitted verified calculations showing otherwise. Further, basic customs duty serves a different 
purpose and cannot replace anti-dumping duty. The existing measure also does not prohibit imports. 
The Authority therefore finds no sufficient reason to change its findings or accept the remaining 
requests, as they relate to earlier proceedings or matters outside the scope of the present review. 


N. CONCLUSION 


Having considered the investigation record, the disclosed facts and the comments received thereon, 
the Authority concludes as follows: 


The product under consideration and the existing CKD/SKD coverage remain unchanged. 
York Transport Equipment (India) Pvt. Ltd. qualifies as the domestic industry for the 
purposes of Rule 2(b). 


Dumping continued during the period of investigation despite the duty in force. The 
Authority has also found positive price undercutting in the absence of anti-dumping duty. 


The domestic industry’s positive performance under the existing measure does not remove 
the likelihood of injury on its expiry. The evidence concerning available capacity, export 
orientation, lower third-country prices, continuing imports and likely price effects 
establishes a likelihood of continuation or recurrence of dumping and injury. 


The Authority has examined other factors that may have affected the performance of the domestic 
industry. After considering the post-disclosure comments and the evidence on record, the 
Authority finds no sufficient reason to change its findings on dumping, injury and the likelihood 
of their continuation or recurrence. Accordingly, the Authority concludes that the requirements for 
continuation of anti-dumping duty under Section 9A(5) read with Rule 23(B) are satisfied.

O. RECOMMENDATIONS 


39. The Authority has duly considered the oral, written and post-disclosure submissions of all interested 
parties, along with the verified evidence on record. Upon comprehensive examination, the Authority 
concludes that expiry of the existing anti-dumping duty is likely to result in continuation or 
recurrence of dumping and consequent injury to the domestic industry. 


40. Since the Authority has recommended continuation of the measure on the basis of the likelihood of 
continuation or recurrence of dumping and injury, it does not consider it appropriate to re-quantify 
the duty in force. Accordingly, the Authority recommends continuation of the definitive anti- 
dumping duty on imports of the product under consideration originating in or exported from China 
PR, at the existing producer-specific rates and country coverage specified in the duty table below, for 
a further period of five (5) years under Section 9A(5) of the Customs Tariff Act, 975, read with 
Rule 23 of the Anti-Dumping Rules, [995, unless revoked, amended or superseded earlier. The

के बीच (कि.मी 3/25-27 पर) स्थित समपार सं. 03 की जगह 4-लेन आरओबी (रेलवे ओवर ब्रिज) के निर्माण के लिए 20A 
अधिसूचना जारी की गई थी. यह अधिसूचना रेल मंत्रालय (दक्षिण मध्य रेलवे), विजयवाड़ा द्वारा एस.ओ. सं. 2277(5) 
(दिनांक 06-05-2026) के तहत जारी की गई थी और भारत के राजपत्र (गजट) में सं. 2186 (नई दिल्‍ली, सोमवार, 
06.05.2026) के रूप में प्रकाशित हुई थी. इसके अलावा, सक्षम प्राधिकारी और राजस्व मंडल अधिकारी, गुंटूर के आर.सी.सं. 
688/2026-J (दिनांक 22-05-2026) के तहत, इसे दो स्थानीय समाचार पत्रों - "वार्ता" (अंग्रेजी संस्करण) और "SATS" 
(तेलुगु संस्करण) में 23-05-2026 को प्रकाशित किया गया था. अब, रेलवे अधिकारियों द्वारा प्रस्तुत संशोधित 'लैंड प्लान 
शेड्यूल' (भूमि योजना अनुसूची) के कारण इस अधिसूचना को वापस ले लिया गया है, क्योंकि पुनर्सविक्षण के दौरान भूमि के 
क्षेत्रफल में कुछ अंतर पाया गया था. इसलिए, नीचे दिए गए विवरण के अनुसार संशोधित 20/ अधिसूचना को मंजूरी दी 
गई है. 


एस.ओ. रेल अधिनियम, 1989 (1989 का 24) (जिसे आगे 'उक्त अधिनियम' कहा गया है) की धारा 20/ की उप-धारा (1) 
द्वारा प्रदत्त शक्तियों का प्रयोग करते हुए, केंद्र सरकार इस बात से संतुष्ट होने के बाद कि आंध्र प्रदेश के गुंटूर जिले में गुंट्र और

भूमि की आवश्यकता है, जिसका संक्षिप्त विवरण इसके साथ संलग्न अनुसूची में दिया गया है, एतट्टारा ऐसी भूमि का अधिग्रहण 
करने के अपने इरादे की घोषणा करती है. 


उक्त भूमि में रुचि रखने वाला कोई भी व्यक्ति उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 20-( 0) की उप-धारा (1) के तहत 
आधिकारिक राजपत्र में इस अधिसूचना के प्रकाशन की तिथि से तीस (30) दिनों की अवधि के भीतर उपरोक्त उद्देश्य के लिए 
ऐसी भूमि के अधिग्रहण और उपयोग पर आपत्ति उठा सकता है. 

इस तरह की हर आप त्ति सक्षम प्राधिकारी, यानी Wax जिले के राजस्व मंडल अधिकारी (रेवेन्यू डिविजनल ऑफिसर) 
के पास लिखित रूप में दर्ज कराई जानी चाहिए, जिसमें आपत्ति के आधार भी बताए जाने चाहिए. सक्षम प्राधिकारी (राजस्व 
मंडल अधिकारी, गुंटूर) आपत्ति करने वाले को स्वयं या किसी कानूनी सलाहकार के माध्यम से अपनी बात रखने का मौका 
देंगे. सभी आपत्तियों को सुनने और अपनी जरूरत के अनुसार आगे की जांच-पड़ताल करने के बाद, सक्षम प्राधिकारी एक 
आदेश जारी करके इन आपत्तियों को स्वीकार या अस्वीकार कर सकते हैं. 


उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 20-(0) की उप-धारा (॥) के अंतर्गत सक्षम प्राधिकारी द्वारा दिया गया कोई भी आदेश 
अंतिम होगा. 


इस अधिसूचना के अंतर्गत आने वाली भूमि के नक्शे और अन्य विवरण उपलब्ध हैं, और इच्छुक व्यक्ति सक्षम 
प्राधिकारी के उक्त कार्यालय में जाकर इन्हें देख सकते हैं.

Divisional Officer, Guntur was withdrawn due to revised Land Plan Schedules submitted by the Railway

approved as hereunder. 


9.0 In exercise of the power conferred by sub-section (1) of Section 20A of the Railways Act, 1989 (24 
of 1989) (hereinafter referred to as the said Act), the Central Government after being satisfied that the land, 
the brief description of which is given in the Schedule annexed hereto, is required for construction of Road 
Over Bridge in lieu of Level Crossing No.03 at Km 3/25-27 between Guntur and Nambur in Guntur District 
of Andhra Pradesh, hereby declares its intention to acquire such land. 


Any person interested in the said land may raise objection to the acquisition and use of such land for 
the aforesaid purpose under sub-section (1) of Section 20-D of the said Act within a period of thirty (30) days 
from the date of publication of this notification in the official gazette. 


Every such objection shall be made to the Competent Authority, namely Revenue Divisional Officer 
Guntur, Guntur District in writing and shall set out the grounds thereof and the Competent Authority and 
Revenue Divisional Officer, Guntur of Guntur District shall give the objector an opportunity of being heard, 
either in person or by legal practitioner and may, after hearing all such objections and after making such 
further enquiry, if any as the Competent Authority thinks necessary, by order, either allow or disallow the 
objections. 


Any order made by the Competent Authority under sub section (1) of section 20-(D) of the said act 
shall be final. 


The land plans and other details of the land under this notification are available and can be inspected 
by the interested persons at the aforesaid office of the competent authority.

जिन्होंने लाइसेंस प्राप्त करने के बाद, किसी कारण से वास्तव में अफीम पोस्ता की खेती नहीं करते हैं, वे फसल वर्ष 
2027-28 के लिए पोस्ता भूसा, जिससे लान्सिंग के माध्यम से कोई रस नहीं निकाला जाता है, के उत्पादन के 
लिए अफीम पोस्ता की खेती के लिए पात्र होंगे।

फसल AT 2026-27 के दौरान अफीम गोंद के उत्पादन के लिए अफीम ea की खेती के लिए लाइसेंस जारी 
करने के लिए पात्र किसानों को आवेदन पत्र संख्या । में भूखंड के मालिक का विवरण, उस भूखंड की सर्वेक्षण 
संख्या आदि देनी होगी जिसमें वे अफीम area की फसल उगाने का इरादा रखते हैं और साथ ही नारकोटिक्स 
आयुक्त द्वारा निर्देशित कोई अन्य विवरण भी देना होगा। 


ये सामान्य लाइसेंसिंग शर्तें स्‍्वापक औषधि एवं मनः:प्रभावी पदार्थ अधिनियम, 985 और उसके अधीन बनाए 
गए नियमों के प्रावधानों के अनुसार, जब भी उचित समझा जाए, स्वापक आयुक्त/ स्वापक उप-आयुक्त के लाइसेंस 
जारी करने/रोकने के अधिकार पर प्रतिकूल प्रभाव डाले बिना है। 


लाइसेंस इस शर्त पर दिया जाएगा कि किसी भी खेत को सरकार द्वारा अथवा सरकार द्वारा विशिष्ट संस्था अथवा 
एजेंसी के साथ सहयोग करके किये जाने वाले अनुसंधान के प्रयोजनार्थ अधिग्रहित किया जा सकता है। जिस 
किसान के खेतों को अनुसंधान के लिए चुना जाएगा उसका अगले वर्ष लाइसेंस मंजूर करने पर विचार किया 
जाएगा बशर्ते उसने (निर्धारित न्यूनतम ASH) उपज प्रस्तुत की हो और वह अन्यथा पात्र हो। अनुसंधान हेतु चुने 
गए क्षेत्र को उपज की गणना करते समय लेखे में नहीं लिया जाएगा। 

कृषक द्वारा प्रस्तुत अफीम का भुगतान करने के प्रयोजनार्थ, राजकीय अफीम एवं अल्कलॉइड कारखाना, नीमच या 


गाजीपुर द्वारा विश्लेषण के आधार पर, या तो कृषक द्वारा प्रस्तुत अफीम की मात्रा के 70" सांद्रता के आधार पर या 
मार्फीन की मात्रा के आधार पर की जाएगी, यदि सरकार ऐसा करने का निर्णय लेती है। 


ऐसे कृषकों के संबंध में जिनके पास किसी विशेष गांव में अफीम की खेती का लाइसेंस है, लेकिन वे निकटवर्ती गांव 
में निवास करते हैं, ऐसे कृषकों को अपने निवास में अफीम का भंडारण करने की अनुमति दी जा सकती है, बशर्ते 
कि ऐसे गांवों के बीच निरंतर मानव बस्तियां हों। 


पात्र किसानों के नाम सीबीएन वेबसाइट (chn.gov.in) और/या सीबीएन ऑनलाइन पोर्टल 
(cbnonline.gov.in) पर अपलोड किए जाएंगे और दिए गए मोबाइल नंबर पर संदेश, मेल आदि जैसे अन्य 
माध्यमों से सूचित किया जा सकता है। पात्रता सूची में सूचीबद्ध किसान निर्धारित समय सीमा के भीतर लाइसेंस 
प्राप्त करने के लिए सीबीएन ऑनलाइन पोर्टल पर ऑनलाइन मोड के माध्यम से आवेदन करेंगे। 


मौजूदा लाइसेंसधारियों को ऐसे कागजात जमा करने की आवश्यकता नहीं होगी जिसकी जानकारी सीबीएन के 
पास पहले से ही है। पिछले वर्ष से किसी भी परिवर्तन के मामले में जानकारी प्रदान की जाएगी। 


अफीम नीति 2026-27 के हिन्दी संस्करण के किसी पैरा में यदि कोई अंतर हो तो उसका अंग्रेजी संस्करण ही 
अपनाया जाएगा।

New Delhi, the 23rd October, 2026 
No. 0I /2026-Narcotics Control-I 


G.S.R. 92(E).— In pursuance of rule 8 of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances 
Rules, 985, the Central Government hereby notifies the general conditions for grant of license specified 
below for cultivation of opium poppy for obtaining opium gum through lancing on account of the Central 
Government during the Opium Crop Year Commencing on the Ist day of October, 2026 and ending with 
the 30th day of September, 2027. 


l. Place of Cultivation 


Opium poppy cultivation may be licensed in any tract as may be notified in this behalf by the Central 
Government. 


2. Eligibility for Cultivation 


Subject to clauses 3 and 7 of this notification, the following cultivators (including legal heirs) shall be 
eligible for a license to cultivate opium poppy for obtaining opium gum through lancing: 


Cultivators who had cultivated opium poppy during the crop year 2025-26 and tendered an average yield 
of Morphine (MQY-M) not less than 4.4 kg per hectare. 


Note- Average qualifying yield of Morphine in opium tendered in kilograms per hectare will be 
termed as Minimum Qualifying Yield (MQY-M) in the notification hereinafter. 


li. Cultivators who ploughed back their entire poppy crop, cultivated during the crop year, 2023-24, 
2024-25 and 2025-26 under the supervision of the Central Bureau of Narcotics in accordance with 
the provisions in this regard, but had not similarly ploughed back their entire poppy crop during 
2022-23. 


iii. Cultivators whose appeal against refusal of License has been allowed after the last date of 
settlement in the crop year 2025-26. 


iv. Cultivator who is nominated by deceased eligible cultivator in column No. I! in Form No. | (see 
rule 7) for the crop year 2025-26. 


v. One of legal heirs of deceased eligible cultivators as determined by the District Opium Officer after 
following the due process, in the cases where nomination in Form No.! is not made for any reason 
or nomination of person not falling under definition of family members/ blood relatives in Form 
No. | is made. 


3. Conditions of License 


No cultivator shall be granted license unless he/she satisfies that: 


i. He/ She did not, in the course of actual cultivation, exceed the area licensed for poppy cultivation 
during the crop year 2025-26 beyond the 5% ‘Condonable Limit’ allowed in the licensing policy. 


li. He/she did not at any time resort to illicit cultivation of opium poppy and was not charged in any 
competent court for any offence under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 985 
and the Rules made there under.

Morphine content of opium tendered during 2026-27 may become the basis for payment for the

Cultivators who had fully ploughed back their entire poppy during crop year 2024-25 and 2025-26

Cultivators who have fully ploughed back their entire poppy crop in crop year 2026-27 would be

Cultivators who are eligible for a license for cultivation of opium poppy for obtaining opium gum 
through lancing under the opium policy for the crop year 2026-27 but do not obtain license for any 
reason, or who after having obtained a license, do not actually cultivate opium poppy due to any 
reason, would be eligible for cultivation of opium poppy for production of Poppy Straw from 
which no juice is extracted through lancing for the crop year 2027-28. 


6. Condonable Limit: 


If the area actually cultivated is up to 5% in excess of the licensed area, such excess cultivation 


may be condoned.

New Delhi, the 23rd October, 2026 
No. 02 /2026-Narcotics Control-I 


G.S.R. 913(E).— In pursuance of rule 8 of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances 
Rules, 1985, the Central Government hereby notifies the general conditions for eligibility to continue 
cultivation for licensees and grant of license specified below for cultivation of opium poppy for production 
of Poppy Straw from which no juice is extracted through lancing on account of the Central Government 
during the Opium Crop Year Commencing on the 1‘ day of October, 2026 and ending with the 307 day of 
September, 2027. 


1. Place of Cultivation 


Opium poppy cultivation may be licensed in any tract as may be notified in this behalf by the Central 
Government. 


2. Eligibility for Cultivation 


Subject to clauses 3 and 8 of this notification, the following cultivators (including their legal heirs) shall be 
eligible for a license to cultivate opium poppy for production of Poppy Straw from which no juice is 
extracted through lancing: 


1. Cultivators who, on the basis of licenses issued to them, had cultivated opium poppy for production 
of Poppy Straw from which no juice is extracted through lancing during the crop year 2025-26 and 
have tendered an average yield of un-lanced poppy straw 800 kgs per Hectare or above at 
weighment center and have not been debarred from cultivation of opium poppy on any of the 
ground mentioned in Para 5(ii) of this opium policy. 


Note: Cultivators who have tendered an average yield of un-lanced poppy straw below 800 kgs 
per Hectare during crop year 2025-26 are suspended from opium poppy cultivation during crop 
year 2026-27. However, they will continue to hold license for next crop year and will be eligible 
for cultivation subject to the conditions imposed by policy of that year. 


li. Cultivators whose licenses were suspended for the crop year 2025-26 on account of tendering an 
average yield of un-lanced poppy straw below 800 kgs per Hectare during crop year 2024-25, 
would be eligible for licensing for the crop year 2026-27 subject to the other eligibility conditions.

NOTIFICATION 

Mumbai, the 16th October, 2026 


Under clause 20A of the Railways Act, 1989 (24 of 1989) 


S.O. 5760(E).— In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (1) of Section 20A of the Railways Act, 
1989 (24 of 1989) (hereinafter referred to as the said Act), the Central Government is satisfied that, for a public 
purpose, the land briefly described in the Schedule appended hereto is required for the Execution, maintenance, 
management and operation of the Special Railway Project namely “Itarsi-Nagpur Balance 37 Line” under Central 
Railway in Nagpur District of the State of Maharashtra, the Central Government hereby declares its intention to 
acquire the said land. 


Any person interested in the said land may, within a period of thirty days from the date of publication of this 
notification in the Official Gazette, raise objection to the acquisition and use of such land for the aforesaid purpose 
under sub-section (1) of section 20D of the said Act. 


Every such objection shall be made to the Competent Authority namely, Sub-Divisional Officer and Land 
Acquisition Officer, Nagpur (Gramin), in writing and shall set out the grounds thereof, and the Competent 
Authority shall give the objector the opportunity of being heard, either in person or by legal practitioner and may, after 
hearing such objections and after making such further enquiry, if any, as the Competent Authority thinks necessary, by 
order, either allow or disallow the objections. 


Any order made by the Competent Authority under sub-section (2) of section 20D of the said Act shall be 
final. 


The land plans and other details of the land covered under this notification are available and can be inspected 
by the interested person at the aforesaid office of the Competent Authority.

Mumbai, the 21st October, 2026 
Under clause 20E of the Railways Act, 1989 (24 of 1989) 
S.O. 5766(E).— Whereas, by the notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of Railways (Railway 
Board), number, S.O 5549 (E) dated 017 December 2025 published in Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, section 
3 Sub-section (ii), dated the 02"! December 2025 (hereinafter referred to as the said notification) and issued under sub- 
section (1) of section 20A of the Railway Act, 1989 (24 of 1989) (hereinafter referred to as the said Act), the Central 
Government declares its intention to acquire the land specified in the schedule annexed to the said notification for the 
purpose of execution, maintenance, management and operation of Special Railway Project, namely “Manmad-Indore 
New Line (New Line between Manmad to New Dhule and Nardana to Dr. Ambedkar Nagar (309.43 Kms)” in the 
District of Nashik & Dhule of Maharashtra State & Badwani, Khargone, Dhar & Indore District of Madhya 
Pradesh State. 


And whereas, the substance of the said notification was published in for Sub-Divisional Officer (R) & Land 
Acquisition Officer, Dr. Ambedkar Nagar (Mhow) Madhya Pradesh in daily newspapers namely “Dainik Bhaskar” 
& “Free Press Journal” Dated 28-02-2026 under sub section (4) of section 20A of the said Act. 


And whereas, objections were received and the same have been considered by the competent authority 


accordingly orders have been passed. 


And whereas, in pursuance of sub-section 20E of the said Act, the competent authority has submitted its report 


to the Central Government. 


Now therefore, upon receipt of the report of the Competent Authority and in exercise of the powers conferred 
by sub-section (1) of section 20E of the said Act, the Central Government hereby declares that the lands specified in the 


schedule annexed here to shall be acquired for the aforesaid purpose.

प्राधिकारी नोट करते हैं कि पाटनरोधी शुल्क का प्राथमिक उद्देश्य पाटन की अनुचित व्यापार पद्धतियों द्वारा घरेलू 
उद्योग को पहुंचाई गई क्षति को दूर करना है, ताकि भारतीय बाजार में खुली और न्यायसंगत प्रतिस्पर्धा का 
वातावरण विकसित हो सके। यह केवल एक विनियामक उपाय नहीं है, बल्कि राष्ट्रीय हित का विषय है। पाटनरोधी 
उपायों का अधिरोपण आयातों को कम करने के लिए अभिप्रेत नहीं है। बल्कि, यह समान अवसर सुनिश्चित करने का 
एक तंत्र है। प्राधिकारी यह स्वीकार करते हैं कि पाटनरोधी शुल्क को जारी रखने से भारत में उत्पाद के कीमत स्तर 
प्रभावित हो सकते हैं। तथापि, यह नोट करना महत्वपूर्ण है कि इन उपायों को जारी रखने से भारतीय बाजार में 
उचित प्रतिस्पर्धा का सार अप्रभावित रहेगा। प्रतिस्पर्धा को कम करने के बजाय, पाटनरोधी उपाय पाटन पद्धतियों 
के माध्यम से अनुचित लाभ की प्राप्ति को रोकने का कार्य करते हैं। वे संबद्ध वस्तु के व्यापक चयन तक उपभोक्ताओं 
की पहुंच की रक्षा करते हैं। इस प्रकार, पाटनरोधी शुल्क बाधक नहीं हैं, बल्कि उचित व्यापार पद्धतियों के 
सुविधाप्रदाता Sl इस संबंध में, माननीय उच्चतम न्यायालय ने रिलायंस इंडस्ट्रीज लिमिटेड बनाम निर्दिष्ट प्राधिकारी 
एवं अन्य मामले में यह टिप्पणी की कि पाटन से अल्पावधि में कम कीमतों के कारण उपभोक्ताओं को अस्थायी लाभ 
प्राप्त हो सकते हैं, किंतु दीर्घावधि में यह घरेलू उद्योग और बाजार में प्रतिस्पर्धा पर प्रतिकूल प्रभाव डाल सकता है।

Under Article .3 of the Anti-Dumping Agreement and Section 9A(5) of the Act, duties are to be 
continued where the Authority determines that expiry of duty is likely to lead to continuation or 
recurrence of dumping and injury. There is no requirement to establish any ‘exceptional’ circumstance. 


The CESTAT in All India Laminated Fabrics Manufacturers Association vs. DA held that the duties can 
be continued if the Authority, having conducted rigorous investigation, found likelihood of continuation 
or recurrence of dumping and injury. 


The Authority has continued duties in second, third and fourth sunset reviews in several cases, such as 
Acrylic Fibre, Caustic Soda, Phenol, Melamine, PTFE, Nylon Tyre Cord Fabric, etc. In fact, various 
other jurisdictions have also extended duties for more than 20 years, where warranted. 


The present duties are in the form of a reference price fixed on the basis of the cost and price conditions 
of January—-December 20l4. The landed price of the subject imports during the POI is above the 
reference price but below the current non-injurious price for PCNs A-l-5 and A-l-6, and as long as 
imports are priced marginally above the reference price, they continue to cause injury. The reference 
price form has thus been rendered ineffective. 


While the request for modification of form and quantum of duty was not accepted in the previous 
review, the facts and circumstances of the present case are different and warrant such modifications. 


The Authority has modified the form of duty from reference price to fixed duty in the past (Caustic 
Soda, CPVC, Measuring Tapes, Melamine, MDF, PTFE, Phenol, Sodium Nitrite, Viscose Filament 
Yarn). The Authority has also enhanced the quantum of duty in sunset reviews (Caustic Soda, PTFE, 
Atrazine (CVD), Glass Fibre). 


The exporters in the subject country are resorting to unfair selling practices in order to avoid payment of 
duties. 


Since the reference price duty is triggered only if the price of imports is lower than the fixed limit, the 
Chinese exporters are declaring an export price which is marginally higher than the benchmark 
determined by the Authority, in order to avoid paying the anti-dumping duties. 


However, such price is only being declared at the Customs port and is not the price which is offered to 
the customers. The actual price offered to the customers is much lower than the price declared at 
customs port. 


Such low-priced imports are eventually entering the market and competing with the domestic industry. 


The Chinese exporters are also resorting to transshipment of subject goods through third countries such 
as the UAE and Singapore. 


Detailed market research reports submitted show that there are no production facilities in such countries 
and all exports are being made only through traders. 


Significant volume of exports in absence of any production facilities clearly shows that the traders in 
third countries are selling Chinese goods to avoid duty payment. 


The volume and price of such imports should be considered as part of subject imports. 


The duty should be denominated in US$/MT, since exporters transact in US$; duty in INR would be

the Act and Rule 23(/B) of the Rules, consistent with Article l.3 of the Anti-Dumping Agreement, provide 
that the duty shall cease after five years unless the Authority, in a review, comes to the conclusion that the 
expiry of duty is likely to lead to continuation or recurrence of dumping and injury. Neither the statute nor the

exporters, the Authority notes that determination of origin of the goods at the transaction level is a matter 
falling within the domain of the Customs authorities under the Customs Act, 962. The Authority has, for the 
purpose of the present determination, considered as subject imports only those imports recorded as originating 
in China PR. The domestic industry is at liberty to approach the Authority under Rule 25 of the Rules with duly 
substantiated evidence of circumvention. 


The domestic industry has requested for change in the form of duty in order to remedy the continued injury 
being caused by the dumped imports. The anti-dumping duty presently in force is in the form of a reference 
price, whereby duty equal to the difference between the reference price and the landed value of the imports is 
levied where the landed value is below the reference price. The domestic industry has submitted that the 
present duties have been ineffective in remedying the continued imports in significant volume despite duties in 
place for 0 years. Further, the domestic industry has claimed that due to the benchmark form of the duty, the 
Chinese exporters have aligned their prices to the reference price notified by the Authority. As such, the import 
prices being declared at the Customs port is at the level or slightly above the reference price, while the actual 
re-sale price offered to customers in the market is much lower. As a result, the domestic industry has contended 
that it has continued to face injury due to presence of low-priced imports. The other interested party has 
claimed that the form should not be modified since duties in the form of reference price was imposed at the 
request of the domestic industry. It has also been added that in case the duty is modified, JSC being the sole 
cooperative producer, should be given an individual rate. 


The Authority notes that the reference price now in force was set on the cost and price conditions of the 
original period of investigation (January—December 204). Those conditions are now more than a decade old. 
The record of the present review shows that most subject imports during the POI entered at landed values at or 
close to the reference price. This suggests that declared import prices may be gravitating towards the reference 
price rather than reflecting conditions in the market. At the same time, the domestic industry’s performance has 
deteriorated during the injury period, and the volume of subject imports has risen significantly. These facts 
raise a question about whether the present form of duty is still effective in removing the injury. 


The fact that the reference price form was adopted at the domestic industry’s request in the original 
investigation does not bind the Authority in this review. The form of duty is to be decided on the record of the 
present proceedings, and in light of how the measure has actually worked over its life. 


As regards the contention of JSC that the INR depreciation has increased the reference price by about 55% in 
rupee terms, the Authority notes that the exchange rate in the POI of the original investigation was 6.59, while 
the same was 73.l7 in the POI of the previous sunset review. The exchange rate in the present POI is 86.76. 
Thus, the exchange rate is increased by 4!% as compared to original investigation, and by !9% as compared to 
previous sunset review. It is thus incorrect that the change is 55%. Further, the relevant comparison is between 
the landed price of the imports and the current non-injurious price, both of which are determined afresh for the 
POI and in INR terms. Further, the majority of the imports in the present POI are at a price very close to the 
benchmark in place. The Authority also notes that duties denominated in US$ are consistent with its 
established practice, since the export transactions are in US$.

Examination by the Authority 


Market economy treatment and normal value for China PR 
Article 5 of China’s Accession Protocol to the WTO provides as follows: 


“Article VI of the GATT 7994, the Agreement on Implementation of Article VI of the General Agreement 
on Tariffs and Trade 994 ("Anti-Dumping Agreement") and the SCM Agreement shall apply in 
proceedings involving imports of Chinese origin into a WTO Member consistent with the following: 


In determining price comparability under Article VI of the GATT 7994 and the Anti-Dumping 
Agreement, the importing WTO Member shall use either Chinese prices or costs for the industry under 
investigation or a methodology that is not based on a strict comparison with domestic prices or costs in 
China based on the following rules: 


(i) If the producers under investigation can clearly show that market economy conditions prevail in the 
industry producing the like product with regard to the manufacture, production and sale of that product, 
the importing WTO Member shall use Chinese prices or costs for the industry under investigation in 
determining price comparability; 


(ti) The importing WTO Member may use a methodology that is not based on a strict comparison with 
domestic prices or costs in China if the producers under investigation cannot clearly show that market 
economy conditions prevail in the industry producing the like product with regard to manufacture, 
production and sale of that product. 


In proceedings under Parts II, III and V of the SCM Agreement, when addressing subsidies described in 
Articles /4(9), /4(0), /4(०0) and /4(6), relevant provisions of the SCM Agreement shall apply; however, 
if there are special difficulties in that application, the importing WTO Member may then use 
methodologies for identifying and measuring the subsidy benefit which take into account the possibility 
that prevailing terms and conditions in China may not always be available as appropriate benchmarks. 
In applying such methodologies, where practicable, the importing WTO Member should adjust such 
prevailing terms and conditions before considering the use of terms and conditions prevailing outside 
China. 


The importing WTO Member shall notify methodologies used in accordance with subparagraph (a) to 
the Committee on Anti-Dumping Practices and shall notify methodologies used in accordance with 
subparagraph (b) to the Committee on Subsidies and Countervailing Measures. 


Once China has established, under the national law of the importing WTO Member, that it is a market 
economy, the provisions of subparagraph (a) shall be terminated provided that the importing Member's 
national law contains market economy criteria as of the date of accession. In any event, the provisions 
of subparagraph (a)(ti) shall expire 73 years after the date of accession. In addition, should China 
establish, pursuant to the national law of the importing WTO Member, that market economy conditions 
prevail in a particular industry or sector, the non-market economy provisions of subparagraph (a) shall 
no longer apply to that industry or sector.” 


The applicants have cited and relied upon Article l5(a)(i) of China’s Accession Protocol. The applicants have 
claimed that producers in China PR must be asked to demonstrate that market economy conditions prevail in 
their industry producing the like product with regard to production and sale of the product under consideration. 
It has been stated by the applicants that in case the responding Chinese producers are not able to demonstrate

Price effect of dumped imports 


The price effect of the dumped imports has been examined in terms of Para (ii) of Annexure-II to the Customs 
Tariff (Identification, Assessment and Collection of Anti-Dumping Duty on Dumped Articles and for 
Determination of Injury) Rules, 995, which provides as follows: 


“While examining the volume of dumped imports, the said authority shall consider whether there has 
been a significant increase in the dumped imports either in absolute terms or relative to production or 
consumption in India, and with regard to the effect of the dumped imports on prices as referred to in 
sub-rule (2) of rule 6 the designated authority shall consider whether there has been a significant 
price undercutting by the dumped imports as compared with the price of like product in India, or 
whether the effect of such imports is otherwise to depress prices to a significant degree or prevent price 
increase which otherwise would have occurred to a significant degree.” 


A reading of the above provision shows that the price effect of the dumped imports is to be examined with 
reference to three independent and disjunctive parameters, namely (a) significant price undercutting, (b) 
significant price depression, and (c) significant price suppression, i.e. prevention of price increases which 
would otherwise have occurred. The said parameters are connected by the disjunctive expression “or”, and the 
existence of any one of them is sufficient to establish that the dumped imports have had an adverse effect on 
the prices of the domestic industry. The absence of price undercutting in a given period does not, therefore, 
preclude a finding of price depression or price suppression.

sales realisation of the domestic industry, PCN-wise, for the POI. The landed price has been determined on the 
basis of the CIF value as per DG Systems data, with the addition of the applicable basic customs duty and 
social welfare surcharge.

Examination by the Authority 


The present investigation is a sunset review, wherein the Authority is required to examine whether the expiry 
of the anti-dumping duty is likely to lead to continuation or recurrence of dumping and injury. The Rules do 
not prescribe a specific methodology for the likelihood analysis. The Authority has examined the likelihood 
having regard to the factors in Article |l.3 of the Anti-Dumping Agreement and Section 9A(5) of the Act, and 
the factors referred to in Article 3.7 of the Agreement, namely the rate of increase of dumped imports, freely 
disposable capacity of the exporters, prices of imports and inventories, to the extent relevant. The Authority has 
examined all the relevant information brought on record by the domestic industry and the other interested 
parties and has noted as below. 


With regards to the arguments that JSC has not witnessed any large capacity expansions, does not have any idle 
capacities and its exports realization is higher than its domestic prices, the Authority notes that the likelihood 
determination is made with respect to the subject country as a whole. The data of a single exporter accounting 
for about 5% of the subject imports cannot by itself negate the likelihood established on the basis of the 
country-level evidence.

The dumping margins determined for the POI are positive and significant, both for the responding exporter and 
for the other producers/exporters. The dumping margins in the original investigation and first sunset review 
were also significant. The exporters have thus continued to export at dumped prices over a prolonged period, 
and it is likely that dumping would continue, or intensify, in the absence of duty.

Volume and price of imports from third countries

scope is set by the measure under review: the anti-dumping duty in force on imports of the subject goods from

likely to lead to continuation or recurrence of dumping and injury. 


The Authority notes that during the POI, the subject goods were also imported in significant volumes from 
USA, Saudi Arabia, Singapore and UAE at prices below those of the subject imports. These countries are not

Contraction in demand 


. The demand for the subject goods has increased by 23% over the injury period and is not expected to decline.

Changes in the pattern of consumption

Developments in technology

Performance of other products

Productivity

Causal link 


The following parameters establish causal link between the dumped imports and injury to the domestic 
industry. 


a. Despite anti-dumping duties in force, the subject imports have continued to enter the domestic market at 
dumped prices. 


b. The subject imports have increased in absolute terms and in relation to domestic production and 
consumption over the injury period. 


c. Asaresult, the market share of the domestic industry has declined over the injury period, while that of the 
subject imports has increased over the period. 


d. The domestic industry was forced to reduce its selling price at a rate higher than decline in costs, in order 
to compete with the dumped imports. 


e. Asaresult, the domestic industry faced significant decline in its profits and its cash profits declined. 
f. This resulted in the domestic industry earning very low returns on its investment. 


g. While the capacities have remained stable and production has increased, the domestic industry operated at 
very low capacity utilisation. 


In view of the above, the Authority concludes that the injury suffered by the domestic industry is on account of 
the dumped imports from the subject country, and that the other known factors have not caused injury to the 
domestic industry.

Examination by the Authority 


The Authority notes that the primary objective of anti-dumping duties is to rectify the injury inflicted upon the 
domestic industry by the unjust trade practices of dumping, thereby fostering an environment of open and 
equitable competition in the Indian market. This is not merely a regulatory measure, but a matter of national 
interest. The imposition of anti-dumping measures is not designed to curtail imports. Rather, it is a mechanism 
to ensure a level playing field. The Authority acknowledges that the continuation of anti-dumping duties may 
influence the price levels of the product in India. However, it is crucial to note that the essence of fair 
competition in the Indian market will remain unscathed by the continuation of these measures. Far from 
diminishing competition, anti-dumping measures serve to prevent the accrual of unfair advantages through 
dumping practices. They safeguard the consumers' access to a broad selection of the subject goods. Thus, anti- 
dumping duties are not a hindrance but a facilitator of fair-trade practices. In this regard, the Hon'ble Supreme 
Court in Reliance Industries Ltd. v. Designated Authority & Ors. observed that dumping may provide 
transitory benefits to consumers in the short term on account of lower prices, but in the long run may adversely 
affect domestic industry and competition in the market. 


The Authority issued the initiation notification, inviting views from all interested parties including importers, 
users and consumers. An Economic Interest Questionnaire was also prescribed to allow various stakeholders, 
including the domestic industry, producers/exporters and importers/users/consumers to provide relevant 
information concerning the present investigation, including the possible effect of anti-dumping duty on their 
operations. 


The Authority notes that no importer, user or consumer of the subject goods has participated in the present 
investigation or filed an economic interest questionnaire response. 


The domestic industry has submitted that the subject goods are capital goods with a life of 25-30 years used 
predominantly by large corporations in hydrocarbon, refinery, power and boiler sectors. Further, the domestic

downstream users, as can be seen from the table below. Further, since the goods have a life span of up to 30

.2 इन विनियमों का विस्तार केंद्रशासित प्रदेश चंडीगढ़ के उस लाइसेंस प्राप्त क्षेत्र तक होगा, जिसका उल्लेख चंडीगढ़ प्रशासन

समय-समय पर संशोधित, में किया गया है। ये विनियम केंद्रशासित प्रदेश चंडीगढ़ के भीतर चंडीगढ़ पावर डिस्ट्रीब्यूशन 
लिमिटेड (संक्षेप में, सीपीडीएल) द्वारा विद्युत के वितरण एवं खुदरा आपूर्ति पर लागू होंगे। ये विनियम राजपत्र में इनके 
प्रकाशन की तारीख से प्रवृत्त होंगे। 

4.3 इन विनियमों के प्रावधान आयोग के अन्य विनियमों के पूरक होंगे तथा उनकी व्याख्या उन विनियमों के साथ सामंजस्य 
स्थापित करते हुए की जाएगी। ऐसे किसी विषय के संबंध में, जिसके लिए इन विनियमों में विशेष रूप से कोई प्रावधान नहीं 
किया गया है, संयुक्त विद्युत विनियामक आयोग (गोवा राज्य एवं संघ राज्य क्षेत्रों के लिए) (पारेषण एवं वितरण लाइयसेंसिंग) 
विनियम, 2020 के प्रावधान लागू होंगे। 

2. परिभाषाएँ 

2. इन विनियमों में, जब तक कि संदर्भ से अन्यथा अपेक्षित न हो:-- 

(a) “सामान्य st” (General Conditions) से अभिप्राय लाइसेंस की उन शर्तों से है, जो संयुक्त विद्युत विनियामक आयोग 
(गोवा राज्य एवं संघ राज्य क्षेत्रों के लिए) (पारेषण एवं वितरण लाइसेंसिंग) विनियम, 2020 में विनिर्दिष्ट हैं तथा 
लाइसेंसधारी पर लागू होती हैं। 

(b) “विशिष्ट शर्तें” (Specific Conditions) से अभिप्राय लाइसेंस की उन शर्तों से है, जो इन विनियमों में विनिर्दिष्ट हैं तथा 
संबंधित लाइसेंसधारी पर लागू होती हैं। 

2.2 इन विनियमों में प्रयुक्त ऐसे शब्दों एवं अभिव्यक्तियों, जिन्हें इन विनियमों में विशेष रूप से परिभाषित नहीं किया गया 
है, किंतु जिन्हें अधिनियम में परिभाषित किया गया है, के वही अर्थ होंगे जो उन्हें विद्युत अधिनियम, 2003 में दिए गए हैं। 
यदि ऐसे शब्दों एवं अभिव्यक्तियों को अधिनियम अथवा आयोग के विनिययमों में परिभाषित नहीं किया गया है, किंतु संसद 
द्वारा अधिनियमित किसी अन्य विधि में परिभाषित किया गया है तथा वह विधि संबंधित राज्य या संघ राज्य क्षेत्र में विद्युत 
क्षेत्र पर लागू होती है, तो ऐसे शब्दों एवं अभिव्यक्तियों के वही अर्थ होंगे जो उक्त विधि में निर्धारित हैं। 

3. प्रयोज्यता 

ये विशिष्ट शर्तें, संयुक्त विद्युत विनियामक आयोग (गोवा राज्य एवं संघ राज्य क्षेत्रों के लिए) (पारेषण एवं वितरण लाइयसेंसिंग) 
विनियम, 2020 तथा समय-समय पर प्रवृत्त वितरण लाइसेंसधारियों पर लागू सामान्य शर्तों के अतिरिक्त, अधिनियम के 
प्रावधानों के अनुसार चंडीगढ़ में पंजीकृत कार्यालय रखने वाली सीपीडीएल॥/ के लाइसेंस की शर्तें मानी जाएँगी। 

4. वितरण क्षेत्र अथवा आपूर्ति क्षेत्र 

4.4 वह आपूर्ति क्षेत्र जिसके भीतर सीपीडीएल विद्युत की आपूर्ति करने के लिए अधिकृत है, केंद्रशासित प्रदेश चंडीगढ़ का 
संपूर्ण भौगोलिक क्षेत्र होगा, जैसा कि चंडीगढ़ प्रशासन द्वारा featH 3.07.2025 तथा 30.07.2026 को जारी अंतरण 
योजना में, यथा समय-समय पर संशोधित, उल्लिखित है। यह क्षेत्र उक्त अधिसूचना में विनिर्दिष्ट शर्तों एवं अपवर्जनों के अधीन

से 25 वर्ष की अवधि के लिए, अर्थात्‌ 3 जनवरी, 2050 तक, अथवा अधिनियम एवं नियमों के अनुसार निरस्त या नवीनीकृत

Gurugram, the 14th October, 2026 


JERC No. 37/2026.—In exercise of power conferred Under Section 91 & 181 of the Electricity Act, 2003 and 
Chapter IV para 18.2 of JERC for the State of Goa & UTs (Recruitment Control and Service Conditions of Officers and 
Staff) Regulations, 2009, and in supersession of the Joint Electricity Regulatory Commission (Medical Facility) 
Regulations 2024, the Joint Electricity Regulatory Commission (JERC) hereby makes the following Regulations: 


1. Short Title, Extent of Application and Commencement 


i. These Regulations may be called the Joint Electricity Regulatory Commission (Medical Facility) Regulations, 
2026. 


ii. The Joint Electricity Regulatory Commission (Medical Facility) Regulations, 2024 stands repealed from the date 
of notification of these Regulations. 


iii. These Regulations shall come into effect from the date of publication in the official Gazette. 


2. Definitions 
In these Regulations, unless the context otherwise requires: - 
1. “Commission” means Joint Electricity Regulatory Commission (For the State of Goa & UTs). 


ii. “Competent Authority” means the Chairperson of the Commission or any other officer to whom such powers 
may be delegated by the Commission for the purpose of these Regulations. 


iii. “Eligible Persons” includes 
e Incumbents appointed against sanctioned posts, regular employees and deputationists of the Commission. 


e Person who has superannuated (at the age of 60 or as decided by the Central Government and adopted by 
the Commission). 


e Medical facilities shall be allowed to the Chairperson and Member under these regulations after completion 
of their tenure or upon attaining the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier. During their tenure, their medical 
facilities shall be regulated as per Rule 13 of the Ministry of Power Notification dated 19.03.2007. 


e Employees in case of his/her retirement on medical incapacitation before superannuation shall also be 
eligible to avail the benefit under these regulations. Employees in case of his/her voluntary retirement by 
giving notice of not less than three months in writing to the Commission after he/she has rendered at least 
10 years of regular service, in aggregate, in Government / PSUs / Statutory Bodies out of which he/she has 
rendered at least 5 years of regular service in the Commission as on the date of voluntary retirement. 


e Incase of death, irrespective of length of service, the spouse/ dependent family members become eligible 
immediately and may opt for the scheme as per entitlement of the deceased employee. 


iv. Employees who are separated by way of removal or dismissal because of disciplinary proceedings are not 
eligible. 


v. The term 'family' means and includes 


e Husband or wife, as the case may be and other dependant family members. Dependent Family Members 
include: parents (employee can have either his/her parents or his/her parents-in-law as dependents), 
widowed sisters, widowed daughters, minor brothers and minor sister, children and step-children wholly 
dependent upon the Government Servant and who are normally residing with the Government Servant 
(son up to the age of 25 or till his marriage whichever is earlier and daughter till she gets married). In 
addition, ‘dependent’ also includes, dependent divorced /separated daughters (including their dependant 
minor children). 


e The term dependent means that income from all sources, including pension benefit, is less than Rs. 15,000 
per month. However, the spouse of the primary cardholder is an exception to the aforementioned clause.

Procedure for availing Indoor and outdoor treatment 


Outdoor Treatment (OPD) 


The eligible person will be entitled to actual reimbursement of medical expenses for OPD treatment for 
themselves, spouse and their family members with the annual limits based on the last cell of the corresponding 
pay matrix + dearness allowance in which they are /were working, applicable from April to March every 
financial year. The pay scale/pay matrix shall stand revised on implementation of the respective Central Pay 
Commission. 


OPD treatment includes doctor’s consultations, medicine, tests and investigations, daycare procedures, dental 
care, eye care, denture including dental implants, hearing aid (within the overall annual limit) and spectacles 
prescribed by the treating specialist for self and dependent family members. 


This annual limit is exclusive of the expenses incurred on major tests where the cost of such tests is 7,500/- or 
more such as MRI, CT scan, Angiography etc., which will be reimbursable on an actual basis. The said limit 
may be revised by the Commission through a separate order/instructions.

recovery or for the prevention of serious deterioration in the condition of the patient having regard to the nature 
of the disease. The amount to be reimbursed for such special nursing shall be limited to the amount which is in 
excess of 25% of the pay of the eligible person for the period for which special nursing was necessary. For this 
purpose, a certificate/prescription from the health care centre where treatment is undergoing, to be produced. 


The eligible person, subscribed to an insurance policy, is allowed to claim reimbursement from either through 
the insurance company or this Commission or from both sources, subject to condition that the reimbursement 
shall not exceed the total expenditure incurred by the eligible person or dependent family members on the 
treatment. In such case, the reimbursement from the Commission shall be restricted to the claim not paid by 
the Insurance Company, if any or not claimed from the Insurance company as the case may be.

they, as well as eligible dependants, may be allowed to avail of the medical facility according to his/her status. For 
this purpose, they should furnish a joint declaration as to who will prefer the claim for reimbursement of medical 
expenses incurred on the medical attendance and treatment in respect of wife/husband and their dependents. 


Cases where the family stays outside Headquarters (Station) 


Where the family of the eligible person does not reside at the same place where the eligible person is posted, they 
may avail of medical treatment at their normal place of stay, and the expenditure incurred on such treatment shall 
be reimbursed by the Commission. 


In case of critical diseases eligible persons or dependent family members may take IPD treatment in any Health 
Care centre in India which is considered or have a reputation of specialization in treating those critical diseases 
in a better way. However, in such cases prior approval of the Commission shall be obtained. 


Eligible person or dependent family members falling ill at a place other than his/her headquarters are also entitled 
to reimbursement of medical expenses on the same basis as above. 


9. Dental treatment: 


Eligible person and their family members shall be entitled to have ‘dental treatment’ from any dental surgeon/clinic. 


Dental treatments, like Tooth extractions, root canal treatment, scaling, implants, dentures and crowns are 
reimbursable. 


Cosmetic dental treatment like teeth whitening, Dental Veneers, Composite Bonding, tooth-coloured, Laser 
or surgical reshaping of uneven or excess gum tissue to balance a smile shall not be reimbursed. 


Cosmetic dental treatment necessitated by an accident shall be reimbursable. 


10. Reimbursement of purchase of artificial Appliances 


Reimbursement of expenses for purchase/ replacement/repair/ adjustment of various artificial appliances shall be 
allowed. In the case of diseases like Polio, where an appliance is fitted to a child, which has to be readjusted or 


replaced periodically as the child grows or the affected part improves, reimbursement of cost of boot (shoe) in the 


case of such patients is permissible if certified as essential by a specialist in the concerned speciality in the hospitals. 
The expenditure on reimbursement of purchase of artificial Appliances shall be considered as IPD treatment. 


11. Other Conditions 


i. 


The competent authority in the Commission shall be empowered to disallow any claims or part of the claim 
which does not satisfy the required condition for such claim.

eligible person or to their family members shall be reimbursed as per actual, over and above the limit. 


Ambulance Charges 


Ambulance charges for admission to the hospital in case of maternity or serious illness, emergency cases or injury 
shall be reimbursed on actuals. In case public transport such as Taxi has been used to carry the patient in emergency 
or non-availability of Ambulance, actual charges paid shall be reimbursed. 


Medical termination of pregnancy 


The expenditure incurred on medical termination of pregnancy shall be reimbursed in full provided it has been 
performed at a Health Care Centre recognised or approved under the Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act 1971. 


Annual Medical Health check-up 


The eligible person (excluding family) may undergo an annual medical examination in a financial year from the 
empanelled/ nominated health care centre. The expenditure on this will be reimbursed subject to the overall ceiling 
limit as laid down in Regulation 3(i). 


Power to review 


The power to review these Regulations shall vest with the Commission. 


Interpretation 
If any queries is arises on the interpretation of any clause or clauses of these Regulations, it shall be referred to the 
Commission, whose decision shall be final. 


Power to relax and amend 


Where the Chairperson of the Commission is of the view that it is necessary or expedient so to do, he/she may, for 
reasons to be recorded in writing, relax any of the provisions of these Regulations. The Commission reserves the 
right to amend or modify the guidelines of these Regulations in part or in full.
